title.en: Volume 89 Biographies 27: Su Baoheng, Di Yonggu, Wei Ziping, Meng Hao relative: Tianjue, Liang Su, Yi Lazao, Yi Lazijing
title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第二十七: 蘇保衡 翟永固 魏子平 孟浩附:田瑴 梁肅 移剌慥 移剌子敬 Volume 89 Biographies 27: Su Baoheng, Di Yonggu, Wei Ziping, Meng Hao relative: Tianjue, Liang Su, Yi Lazao, Yi Lazijing

sentences.zh: 蘇保衡

translations.literal: Su Baoheng
translations.idiomatic: Su Baoheng

sentences.zh: 蘇保衡，字宗尹，雲中天成人。

translations.literal: Su Baoheng, style name Zongyin, was a native of Zhongtian in Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Su Baoheng, whose style name was Zongyin, came from Zhongtian in the Yun region.

sentences.zh: 父京，遼進士，為西京留守。

translations.literal: His father Jing was a Liao jinshi and served as Western Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su Jing had passed the Liao civil examination and held the post of garrison commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 宗翰兵至西京，京出降。

translations.literal: When Zonghan's army reached the Western Capital, Jing came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Zonghan's army reached the Western Capital, Jing surrendered.

sentences.zh: 久之，京病篤，以保衡屬宗翰。

translations.literal: After some time Jing's illness grew grave, and he entrusted Baoheng to Zonghan.
translations.idiomatic: In time Jing fell gravely ill and entrusted Baoheng to Zonghan's care.

sentences.zh: 京死，宗翰薦之於朝。

translations.literal: When Jing died, Zonghan recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing died, Zonghan recommended him at court.

sentences.zh: 賜進士出身，補太子洗馬，調解州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He was granted jinshi status, appointed Crown Prince attendant, and transferred to be military administrator of Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted jinshi standing, appointed attendant to the crown prince, and transferred to serve as military administrator of Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左監軍撒離喝駐軍陝西，辟幕府，參議軍事，累官同知興中尹。

translations.literal: The Left Overseer Saliahe stationed troops in Shaanxi, recruited him to his staff, had him deliberate on military affairs, and he rose in office to acting prefect of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Left Overseer Saliahe garrisoned Shaanxi, he recruited Baoheng to his staff as a military adviser; Baoheng rose through successive posts to acting prefect of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 天德間，繕治中都，張浩舉保衡分督工役。

translations.literal: During the Tiande era, when the Central Capital was being repaired, Zhang Hao recommended Baoheng to share supervision of the labor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande period, while the Central Capital was being rebuilt, Zhang Hao recommended Baoheng to help supervise the work crews.

sentences.zh: 改大興少尹，督諸陵工役。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice prefect of Daxing and supervised labor at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice prefect of Daxing and put in charge of construction at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 再遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 海陵治兵伐宋，與徐文等造舟於通州，海陵獵近郊，因至通州視工作。

translations.literal: Emperor Hailing prepared troops to attack Song; with Xu Wen and others he built boats at Tongzhou. Hailing hunted in the nearby suburbs and thereby went to Tongzhou to inspect the work.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Hailing mustered forces to invade the Song, he and Xu Wen and others built warships at Tongzhou; on a hunt in the nearby suburbs he went on to Tongzhou to inspect the shipyards.

sentences.zh: 兵興，保衡為浙東道水軍都統制，率舟師泛海，徑趨臨安。

translations.literal: When war arose, Baoheng became overall commander of the Zhedong Circuit naval forces, leading the fleet across the sea straight toward Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities began, Baoheng was made overall commander of the Zhedong naval forces and led the fleet by sea straight for Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來襲，敗於海中，副統制鄭家死之。

translations.literal: Song forces came to attack; they were defeated at sea, and the deputy commander Zheng Jia died.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces attacked; the fleet was defeated at sea, and the deputy commander Zheng Jia was killed.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，召赴中都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was summoned to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dading era he was summoned to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東盜賊嘯聚，契丹攻掠臨潢等州郡，百姓困弊。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were gathering and roaring in Shandong, and the Khitan raided Linhuang and other prefectures; the people were exhausted and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were gathering across Shandong, Khitan forces were raiding Linhuang and neighboring prefectures, and the common people were in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 詔保衡安撫山東，前太子少保高思廉安撫臨潢，發倉粟以賑之，無衣者賜以幣帛，或官粟有闕，則收糴以給之，無妻室者具姓名以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Baoheng to pacify Shandong and the former Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Gao Silian to pacify Linhuang; they opened granaries to relieve the people, gave cloth to those without clothing, and where official grain was insufficient bought grain to supply them; those without wives or households were to have their names reported.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng was ordered to pacify Shandong and the former Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Gao Silian was sent to pacify Linhuang. They opened granaries for relief, gave cloth to the destitute, and where official stores ran short bought grain on the market to make up the deficit; men without wives or families were to be listed by name and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 還除刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 與工部尚書宗永、兵部侍郎完顏余裏也，往河南、山東、陝西宣問屯田軍人，有曾破大敵及攻城野戰立功者，具姓名以聞。

translations.literal: Together with Minister of Works Zong Yong and Vice Minister of War Wanyan Yuliye, he went to Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi to announce inquiries among garrison and military colonists; those who had once broken a great enemy or achieved merit in storming cities or field battle were to have their names reported.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Minister of Works Zong Yong and Vice Minister of War Wanyan Yuliye, he toured Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi to review garrison troops and military colonists; anyone who had defeated a major enemy force or distinguished himself in assaults or field battles was to be named and reported.

sentences.zh: 或以寡敵眾，或與敵相當能先登敗敵者，正軍及擐甲阿裏喜補官一階，猛安謀克以功狀上尚書省，曾隨海陵軍至淮上破敵者亦准上遷賞。

translations.literal: Whether by using few against many or by matching the enemy and being first to ascend and defeat the foe, regular troops and armored Alixi were to receive one step in rank; meng'an and mouke were to send merit reports up to the Ministry, and those who had followed Hailing's army to the Huai and broken the enemy were also allowed promotion and reward on report.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had fought few against many, or matched the enemy and been first over the wall to rout them, were to advance one rank in the regular army or among armored Alixi auxiliaries; meng'an and mouke commanders were to file merit reports with the Ministry, and those who had followed Hailing's army to the Huai and defeated the enemy were likewise eligible for promotion and reward.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義伐宋，保衡行戶部於關中，兼糾察，許以便宜，黜守令不法者十餘人。

translations.literal: When Pusann Zhongyi attacked Song, Baoheng acted as Minister of Revenue in Guanzhong and also as inspector, granted discretionary authority; he dismissed more than ten prefectural and county officials for unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Pusann Zhongyi campaigned against the Song, Baoheng served as acting Minister of Revenue in Guanzhong with additional powers of inspection and discretionary authority; he removed more than ten unlawful prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 邠守傅慎微忤用事者，被讒構下獄且死，保衡力救之得免。

translations.literal: The Bin prefect Fu Shenwei offended those in power, was slandered and framed, imprisoned and nearly executed; Baoheng strove to save him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Bin, Fu Shenwei, had offended the men in power; slanderers framed him and he was thrown into prison facing execution, but Baoheng fought to save him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 入為太常卿，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered service as Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and then promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 宋人請和，詔保衡往南京，與僕散忠義斟酌事宜，行之。

translations.literal: When the Song sought peace, an edict ordered Baoheng to Nanjing to consult with Pusann Zhongyi on the arrangements and carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song sued for peace, Baoheng was ordered to Nanjing to work out the terms with Pusann Zhongyi and put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 入奏，進右丞。

translations.literal: He entered to report and was advanced to Right Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to report to the throne and was promoted to right vice councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，宋人請和，師還，保衡朝京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Song sought peace, the army returned, and Baoheng attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the Song made peace and the army withdrew, Baoheng came to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，宮女稱心縱火十六位，延燒諸殿，上以方用兵，國用不足，不復營繕。

translations.literal: Earlier the palace woman Chengxin had set fire to the Sixteen Offices and the blaze spread through the halls; because the emperor was at war and state funds were insufficient, the palaces were not rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the palace woman Chengxin had set fire to the Sixteen Offices and the flames had spread through the halls; with war underway and the treasury strained, the emperor had not rebuilt them.

sentences.zh: 及宋和，詔保衡監護役事，遣少府監張仲愈取南京宮殿圖本。

translations.literal: When peace was made with Song, an edict ordered Baoheng to oversee the work and sent the Supervisor of the Palace Workshops Zhang Zhongyu to fetch architectural plans of the Nanjing palaces.
translations.idiomatic: After peace with the Song, Baoheng was ordered to supervise reconstruction and Zhang Zhongyu of the Palace Workshops was sent to obtain plans of the Nanjing palaces.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，謂保衡曰：「追仲愈還。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he said to Baoheng: "Recall Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he told Baoheng, "Recall Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 民間將謂朕效正隆華侈也。」

translations.literal: The people will say that I am imitating the Zhenglong era's splendor and extravagance."
translations.idiomatic: The people will say I am copying the lavish excess of the Zhenglong reign."

sentences.zh: 六年冬，有疾，求致仕，不許。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he fell ill and asked to retire; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year he fell ill and asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遣敬嗣暉傳詔曰：「卿以忠直擢居執政，齒發未衰，遽以小疾求退。

translations.literal: Jing Sihui was sent to convey an edict saying: "You were raised to the council for loyalty and uprightness; your teeth and hair are not yet faded—why hurry to withdraw on a minor illness?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sihui was sent with an edict: "You were promoted to the council for your loyalty and integrity; your hair is scarcely gray—why seek retirement over a minor ailment?

sentences.zh: 善加攝養，以俟疾間視事。

translations.literal: Take good care of yourself and wait until the illness passes to resume duties."
translations.idiomatic: Take good care of yourself and wait until you recover before returning to office."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，薨，年五十五。

translations.literal: " Before long he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 世宗將放鷹近郊，聞之乃還，為輟朝，賻贈，命有司致祭。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was about to go hawking in the nearby suburbs; on hearing the news he returned, suspended court, granted funeral gifts, and ordered the relevant offices to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had been about to go hawking in the suburbs; on hearing the news he turned back, suspended court, granted funeral gifts, and ordered the proper offices to conduct the rites.

sentences.zh: 翟永固

translations.literal: Di Yonggu
translations.idiomatic: Di Yonggu

sentences.zh: 翟永固，字仲堅，中都良鄉人。

translations.literal: Di Yonggu, style name Zhongjian, was a native of Liangxiang in the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Di Yonggu, whose style name was Zhongjian, was from Liangxiang in the Central Capital district.

sentences.zh: 太祖與宋約攻遼，事成以燕歸宋。

translations.literal: Taizu made a pact with Song to attack Liao together; when the affair succeeded Yan was to be returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had agreed with the Song to attack the Liao jointly; when the campaign succeeded, the Yan region was to be returned to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宋人以經義兼策取士，永固中第一，授開德府儀曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Song selected scholars by classical learning combined with policy essays; Yonggu placed first and was appointed aide in the ceremonial office of Kaide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song examination combining classical learning with policy essays, Yonggu took first place and was appointed an aide in the ceremonial office of Kaide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金破宋，永固北歸。

translations.literal: When Jin defeated Song, Yonggu returned north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin overran the Song territories, Yonggu returned north.

sentences.zh: 中天會六年詞賦科，授懷安丞，遷望雲令，補樞密院令史，辟左副元帥宗翰府掾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui at Zhongdu he passed the rhapsody and fu examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Huai'an, transferred to magistrate of Wangyun, filled a clerk post in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was recruited as staff to the Left Vice Marshal Zonghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Tianhui era he passed the rhapsody-and-fu examination at Zhongdu, served as assistant magistrate of Huai'an and then magistrate of Wangyun, became a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was recruited to Zonghan's staff as Left Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 永固家貧，求外補，宗翰愛其能，不許，以錢三千貫周之，薦於朝，攝左司郎中。

translations.literal: Yonggu's family was poor; he sought an outside appointment. Zonghan prized his ability and would not allow it, gave him three thousand strings of cash as aid, recommended him to court, and had him act as Left Department director.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu was poor and sought a provincial post, but Zonghan, who valued his talent, refused; he gave him three thousand strings of cash, recommended him at court, and had him serve as acting director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 除定武軍節度副使，曆同知清州防禦使，入為工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy military commissioner of Dingwu Army, served successively as acting prefect of Qingzhou, and entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy military commissioner of the Dingwu army, served as acting prefect of Qing Prefecture, and was recalled to the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官，起複禮部郎中，遷翰林直學士。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning, was recalled to serve as director in the Ministry of Rites, and was transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, was recalled as a director in the Ministry of Rites, and was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，宋國賀正旦使至廣寧，海陵使使以廢立事諭宋使，遣還之。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, the Song New Year's envoy reached Guangning; Hailing sent an envoy to inform the Song envoy of the deposition and enthronement and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing seized the throne, the Song New Year's envoy reached Guangning; Hailing sent a messenger to inform him of the deposition and enthronement and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛親軍都指揮使完顏思恭為報諭宋使，永固為副，且令永固伺察宋人動靜。

translations.literal: The Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guard Wanyan Sigong was made envoy to reply to the Song envoy, with Yonggu as deputy, and Yonggu was also ordered to observe Song movements.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sigong, commander-in-chief of the imperial guard, was sent to reply to the Song envoy with Yonggu as his deputy, and Yonggu was also instructed to watch Song movements.

sentences.zh: 使還，改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was changed to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 久之，分護燕京宮室役事，永固請寫《無逸圖》於殿壁，不納。

translations.literal: After some time he shared supervision of Yanjing palace construction; Yonggu asked to paint the "Against Dissipation" illustration on the hall walls, but this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Later he helped supervise construction of the Yanjing palaces and asked to have the "Against Dissipation" scene painted on the hall walls, but the request was rejected.

sentences.zh: 俄遷太常卿，考試貞元二年進士，出《尊祖配天賦》題，海陵以為猜度己意，召永固問曰：「賦題不稱朕意。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; examining jinshi of the second year of Zhenyuan, he set the topic "Honoring the Ancestor and Matching Heaven"; Hailing thought this guessed at his intentions and summoned Yonggu, asking: "The examination topic does not suit my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; when he set the jinshi examination topic for the second year of Zhenyuan as "Honoring the Ancestor and Matching Heaven," Hailing thought it alluded to his own plans and summoned Yonggu: "The topic does not please me.

sentences.zh: 我祖在位時祭天拜乎？

translations.literal: When my ancestor was on the throne, did he worship Heaven with obeisance?
translations.idiomatic: When my ancestor was on the throne, did he perform obeisance in sacrifices to Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「拜。

translations.literal: " He answered: "He did obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: " Yonggu answered, "He did.

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「豈有生則致拜，死而同體配食者乎？

translations.literal: " Hailing said: "How can there be obeisance in life and sharing the same body in death at the same altar?
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "Can one bow to a living man and then share the sacrificial offering with his corpse?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「古有之，載在典禮。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The ancients had it; it is recorded in the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: " Yonggu replied, "The ancients did so; it is recorded in the ritual codes.

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「若桀、紂曾行，亦欲我行之乎？

translations.literal: " Hailing said: "If Jie and Zhou once practiced it, do you want me to practice it too?
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "If Jie and Zhou did it, do you want me to follow them as well?

sentences.zh: 」於是永固、張景仁皆杖二十。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yonggu and Zhang Jingren were each beaten twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: " Yonggu and Zhang Jingren were each flogged twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 而進士張汝霖賦第八韻有曰：「方今將行郊祀。

translations.literal: The jinshi Zhang Rulin in the eighth rhyme of his fu had the line: "At present suburban sacrifice is about to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The candidate Zhang Rulin wrote in the eighth rhyme of his fu, "At present suburban sacrifice is about to be performed.

sentences.zh: 」海陵詰之曰：「汝安知我郊祀乎？

translations.literal: " Hailing interrogated him: "How do you know I will perform suburban sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing demanded, "How do you know I plan a suburban sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 」亦杖之三十。

translations.literal: " He was also beaten thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: " He too was flogged thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 頃之，永固遷禮部尚書，賜笏頭球文金帶。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Yonggu was transferred to Minister of Rites and granted a golden belt with ball-pattern plaque at the tablet head.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yonggu was made minister of rites and granted a gold belt with ball-pattern plaque at the tablet head.

sentences.zh: 改永定軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to military commissioner of Yongding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Yongding army.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例降二品以上官爵，永固階光祿大夫不降，以寵異之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, by precedent ranks of the second grade and above were reduced; Yonggu's rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was not reduced, as a mark of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong, officials of the second rank and above had their titles reduced by regulation; Yonggu's rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was left unchanged as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士承旨，與直學士韓汝嘉俱召至內殿，問以將親伐宋事，永固對曰：「宋人事本朝無釁隙，伐之無名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor; with Academician Han Rujia he was summoned to the inner hall and asked about personally campaigning against Song. Yonggu answered: "Song has served our dynasty without cause for quarrel; to attack them has no proper name.
translations.idiomatic: He was made expositor of the Hanlin Academy; he and Hanlin academician Han Rujia were summoned to the inner hall and questioned about a personal campaign against the Song. Yonggu replied, "The Song have served our dynasty without provocation; an attack would have no just cause.

sentences.zh: 縱使可伐，亦無煩親征，遣將帥可也。

translations.literal: Even if they could be attacked, there is no need for a personal campaign—send generals and that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they could be attacked, there is no need for Your Majesty to go in person; send generals instead.

sentences.zh: 」由是大忤海陵意，永固即請致仕。

translations.literal: " By this he greatly offended Hailing's intent, and Yonggu at once asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: " This greatly offended Hailing, and Yonggu immediately asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年正月丁巳，海陵朝永壽宮，四品以上官賜宴，永固至殿門外，海陵即以致仕宣命授之，永固歸臥於家。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the first month of the fourth year of Zhenglong, Hailing held court at Yongshou Palace and granted a feast to officials of the fourth rank and above; Yonggu reached the outer palace gate and Hailing at once handed him the retirement edict; Yonggu returned home to lie in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the first month of the fourth year of Zhenglong, Hailing held court at Yongshou Palace and feasted officials of the fourth rank and above; Yonggu came only to the outer gate, where Hailing handed him the retirement edict on the spot, and Yonggu went home to live in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，起拜尚書左丞，請依舊制廉察官吏，革正隆守令之汙，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was recalled and appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; he asked to inspect officials according to the old system and reform the corruption of Zhenglong prefects and magistrates, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was recalled as left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and asked to resume the old system of inspecting officials and cleaning up the corruption of Zhenglong-era prefects and magistrates; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，表乞致仕，詔不許。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized begging to retire; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized asking to retire, but the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 罷為真定尹，賜通犀帶。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be prefect of Zhending and granted a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of the council and made prefect of Zhending, with a rhinoceros-horn belt as a gift.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏，永固自執政為真定尹，其傘蓋當用何制度，上曰：「用執政制度。

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat memorialized: since Yonggu had gone from the council to be prefect of Zhending, what regulations should apply to his parasol and canopy? The emperor said: "Use the council regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Secretariat asked what parasol and canopy regulations Yonggu should use now that he had moved from the council to the prefecture of Zhending. The emperor said, "Use the council regulations.

sentences.zh: 」遂著為令。

translations.literal: " This was then written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: " This was then codified as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 五年，懇乞致仕，許之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he earnestly begged to retire and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he earnestly petitioned to retire and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 六年，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 魏子平

translations.literal: Wei Ziping
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ziping

sentences.zh: 久之，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 上問子平曰：「古者稅什一而民足，今百一而民不足，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Ziping: "In antiquity tax was one in ten and the people were sufficient; today it is one in a hundred and the people are insufficient—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Ziping, "In antiquity a one-tenth levy left the people well provided; today a one-hundredth levy leaves them wanting—why is that?

sentences.zh: 」子平對曰：「什一取其公田之入，今無公田而稅其私田，為法不同。

translations.literal: " Ziping answered: "One in ten took from the revenue of public fields; today there are no public fields yet private fields are taxed—the law is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping replied, "The ancient tenth took only from public-field revenue; today there are no public fields, yet private fields are taxed—the systems differ.

sentences.zh: 古有一易再易之田，中田一年荒而不種，下田二年荒而不種。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were fields of one rotation and two rotations; middle-grade fields left fallow one year were not planted, lower-grade fields left fallow two years were not planted.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity fields were classified for one or two years' fallow; middle-grade land left uncultivated for a year and lower-grade land for two years were not taxed.

sentences.zh: 今乃一切與上田均稅之，此民所以困也。

translations.literal: Now all are taxed equally with the best fields—this is why the people are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Now every plot is taxed at the same rate as the best land—that is why the people are in distress.

sentences.zh: 」上又問曰：「戍卒逋亡物故，今按物力高者補之，可乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor also asked: "When garrison soldiers flee or die, it is now proposed to replace them from households of high assessed property—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also asked, "When garrison soldiers desert or die, is it acceptable to replace them from the wealthiest households by assessed property?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「富家子弟騃懦不可用，守戍歲時求索無厭，家產隨壞。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Sons of rich families are stupid and timid and cannot be used; guarding the garrison they demand without end at the seasons, and family property is ruined in turn.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Sons of rich families are dull and timid and useless in service; on garrison duty they make endless seasonal demands until the family estate is ruined.

sentences.zh: 若按物力多寡賦之，募材勇騎射之士，不足則調兵家子弟補之，庶幾官收實用，人無失職之患。

translations.literal: If levies are assigned according to more or less property, recruiting able and brave men skilled in riding and archery, and when insufficient calling up sons of military families to fill the gap, then perhaps the state will gain real use and people will not suffer the affliction of losing their proper roles.
translations.idiomatic: If the levy were scaled to property and used to recruit able archers and horsemen, with military families called up only when numbers fell short, the state would gain useful soldiers and families would not be ruined by misassigned duty.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 海州捕賊八十餘人，賊首海州人，其兄今為宋之軍官。

translations.literal: Haizhou captured more than eighty bandits; the bandit chief was a Haizhou man, and his elder brother is now a Song military officer.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou captured more than eighty bandits; their leader was a local man whose elder brother now serves as a Song army officer.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，謂宰相曰：「宋之和好，恐不能久，其宿、泗間漢軍，以女直軍代之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it, he told the chief ministers: "Peace with Song probably cannot last long; the Han troops between Su and Si should be replaced with Jurchen troops.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor told his chief ministers, "Peace with the Song may not last; replace the Han troops between Su and Si with Jurchen forces.

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「誓書稱沿邊州城，除自來合設置射糧軍數並巡尉外，更不得屯軍守戍。

translations.literal: " Ziping said: "The oath document states that along the border prefectures and cities, apart from the established numbers of grain-guard archers and patrol officers, no further troops may be stationed on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping said, "The treaty states that along the border prefectures and cities, apart from the established grain-guard archers and patrol officers, no additional garrison troops may be stationed.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此更代之，非增戍也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This is replacement, not increasing the garrison."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "This is a replacement, not an increase in garrison strength."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「前日令內任官六品以上，外任五品以上，並舉所知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The other day I ordered capital officials of the sixth rank and above and provincial officials of the fifth rank and above each to recommend those they knew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The other day I ordered capital officials of the sixth rank and above and provincial officials of the fifth rank and above each to recommend men they knew.

sentences.zh: 未聞有舉之者，豈無其才，蓋知而不舉也。

translations.literal: I have not heard of any recommendations—is there no talent, or do they know but not recommend?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of no recommendations. Is there no talent, or do they know capable men and simply fail to recommend them?

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「請令當舉之官，每任須舉一人。

translations.literal: " Ziping said: "I ask that officials obliged to recommend must recommend one person each term of office.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping said, "Require every official who must recommend talent to nominate at least one person per term of office.

sentences.zh: 」澤州刺史劉德裕、祁州刺史斜哥、滄州同知訛裏也、易州同知訛裏剌、楚丘縣令劉春哥以贓汙抵罪，上欲詔示中外，丞相守道以為不可，上以問子平曰：「卿意何如？

translations.literal: " The Ze Prefecture prefect Liu Deyu, Qi Prefecture prefect Xiege, Cangzhou acting prefect Eliye, Yizhou acting prefect Elila, and Chuqiu county magistrate Liu Chunge were convicted for corruption; the emperor wished to proclaim this within and without, but Chief Councilor Shoudao thought it could not be done. The emperor asked Ziping: "What is your view?
translations.idiomatic: " The prefect of Ze Liu Deyu, the prefect of Qi Xiege, the acting prefect of Cangzhou Eliye, the acting prefect of Yizhou Elila, and the magistrate of Chuqiu Liu Chunge were convicted of corruption. The emperor wished to publish their crimes at home and abroad, but Chief Councilor Shoudao objected. The emperor asked Ziping, "What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「臣聞懲一戒百，陛下固宜行之。

translations.literal: " Ziping said: "I have heard that punishing one warns a hundred—Your Majesty should indeed carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping said, "I have heard that punishing one man warns a hundred—Your Majesty should certainly do this.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It shall be so.

sentences.zh: 」遂降詔焉。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was duly promulgated.

sentences.zh: 宋人于襄陽漢江上造舟為浮梁三，南京統軍司聞而奏之，上問宰臣曰：「卿等度之，以為何如？

translations.literal: The Song built boats on the Han River at Xiangyang and made three pontoon bridges; the Nanjing command heard and memorialized. The emperor asked the chief ministers: "What do you estimate of this?
translations.idiomatic: The Song built boats on the Han River at Xiangyang and laid three pontoon bridges; the Nanjing command reported it, and the emperor asked his ministers, "What do you make of this?

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「臣聞襄陽薪芻，皆於江北取之，殆為此也。

translations.literal: " Ziping said: "I have heard that Xiangyang's firewood and fodder are all taken from north of the river—probably it is for this.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping said, "I have heard that Xiangyang draws all its firewood and fodder from the north bank of the river—this is probably why.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕與卿等治天下，當治其未然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I and you govern the realm—we should govern what is not yet so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You and I govern the realm; we should act before trouble appears.

sentences.zh: 及其有事，然後治之，則亦晚矣。

translations.literal: When trouble has already come and only then we govern it, that is also too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until trouble has already come, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 」河南統軍使宗敘求入見奏邊事，上使修起居注粘割斡特剌就問狀。

translations.literal: " The Henan commander Zong Xu requested an audience to report border affairs; the emperor sent the diarist Jiageduo Wotela to inquire into the facts on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " The Henan commander Zong Xu asked for an audience to report border affairs, and the emperor sent diarist Jiageduo Wotela to investigate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宗敘言：「得邊報及宋來歸者言，宋國調兵募民，運糧餉，完城郭，造戰船浮橋，兵馬移屯江北。

translations.literal: Zong Xu said: "From border reports and persons who have come over from Song it is said that the Song state is mobilizing troops and conscripting people, transporting grain provisions, repairing walls and cities, building warships and pontoon bridges, and moving troops to encamp north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xu reported, "Border reports and defectors from the Song say that the Song are mobilizing troops and conscripts, shipping grain, repairing walls and cities, building warships and pontoon bridges, and moving forces to camps north of the river.

sentences.zh: 自和議後即罷制置司，今複置矣。

translations.literal: Since the peace agreement the Pacification Commission had been abolished; now it has been re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Since the peace treaty the Pacification Commission had been abolished; now it had been restored.

sentences.zh: 商、虢、海州皆有奸人出沒，此不可不備。

translations.literal: Shang, Guo, and Haizhou all had traitors appearing and disappearing—this could not go unprepared for.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors were active in Shang, Guo, and Haizhou—this had to be guarded against.

sentences.zh: 嘗報樞密院，彼視以為文移，故欲入見言之。

translations.literal: He had once reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs, but they treated it as routine paperwork, so he wished to enter audience and speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He had reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs, but they treated it as routine paperwork, so he wanted an audience to speak directly.

sentences.zh: 」斡特剌召凡言邊事者詰問，皆無實狀，行至境上，問知襄陽浮橋乃樵采之路，如子平策。

translations.literal: " Wotela summoned all who spoke of border affairs and interrogated them; none had real substance. Reaching the frontier, he inquired and learned the Xiangyang pontoon bridges were paths for gathering firewood—just as Ziping had surmised.
translations.idiomatic: " Wotela summoned everyone who had reported border troubles and questioned them; none had substance. At the frontier he learned that the Xiangyang pontoon bridges were only firewood-gathering routes, exactly as Ziping had guessed.

sentences.zh: 還奏。

translations.literal: He returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and reported.

sentences.zh: 詔凡妄說邊關兵事者徒二年，告人得實，賞錢五百貫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that whoever falsely spoke of border military affairs was to be sentenced to two years' penal service; informers whose reports proved true were rewarded five hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sentenced anyone who falsely reported border military affairs to two years' penal service and offered five hundred strings of cash to informers whose reports proved true.

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣曰：「祭宗廟用牛。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "In sacrifices to the ancestral temple oxen are used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "Sacrifices to the ancestral temple use oxen.

sentences.zh: 牛盡力稼穡有功於人，殺之何如？

translations.literal: Oxen exhaust their strength in farming and have merit for people—what of killing them?
translations.idiomatic: Oxen exhaust themselves in the fields and do great service to mankind—what of killing them?

sentences.zh: 」子平對曰：「惟天地宗廟用之，所以異大祀之禮也。」

translations.literal: " Ziping answered: "Only for Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple are they used—thereby differing from the rites of great sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: " Ziping replied, "They are used only for Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple, which distinguishes these rites from ordinary great sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 十一年，罷為南京留守，未幾致仕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was dismissed to be Nanjing garrison commander; before long he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was relieved and made Nanjing garrison commander; he retired soon after.

sentences.zh: 十五年，起為平陽尹，複致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled as prefect of Pingyang and again retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled as prefect of Pingyang and retired again.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，薨於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 孟浩，字浩然，濼州人。

translations.literal: Meng Hao, style name Haoran, was a native of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hao, whose style name was Haoran, came from Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 遼末年登進士第。

translations.literal: In the late Liao he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Liao dynasty he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，為樞密院令史，除平州觀察判官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui he was a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed observation administrator of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhui he served as a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs and was appointed observation administrator of Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，選入元帥府備任使，承制除歸德少尹，充行台吏、禮部郎中，入為戶部員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he was selected into the Marshal's Office for assignment, appointed by imperial order as vice prefect of Guide, served as Eastern Secretariat clerk and director in the Ministry of Rites, and entered the capital as vice director and director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianjuan era he was selected for the Marshal's Office, appointed vice prefect of Guide, served on the Eastern Secretariat staff and as a director in the Ministry of Rites, and was recalled to the capital as vice director and then director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 韓企先為相，拔擢一時賢能，皆置機要，浩與田瑴皆在尚書省，瑴為吏部侍郎，浩為左司員外郎。

translations.literal: When Han Qixian was chief minister he promoted the able of the age and placed them in key posts; Hao and Tian Yue were both in the Imperial Secretariat—Yue as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Hao as vice director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qixian was chief minister he promoted the able men of the day to key posts; Hao and Tian Yue both served in the Imperial Secretariat, Yue as vice minister of personnel and Hao as vice director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 既典選，善銓量人物，分別賢否，所引用皆君子。

translations.literal: Once in charge of selection, he was skilled at weighing men and distinguishing worthy from unworthy; those he recommended were all gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In charge of appointments, he was skilled at judging character and distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy; every man he advanced was a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 而蔡松年、曹望之、許霖皆小人，求與瑴相結，瑴薄其為人拒之。

translations.literal: But Cai Songnian, Cao Wangzhi, and Xu Lin were all petty men who sought to ally with Yue; Yue despised their character and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Songnian, Cao Wangzhi, and Xu Lin were petty men who sought an alliance with Yue, but Yue despised them and refused.

sentences.zh: 松年，蔡靖子。

translations.literal: Songnian was the son of Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian was the son of Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 靖將兵不能守燕山，終敗宋國，瑴頗以此譏斥松年，松年初事宗弼於行台省，以微巧得宗弼意，宗弼當國，引為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jing commanded troops but could not hold Yanshan and ultimately ruined the Song state; Yue often used this to ridicule Songnian. Songnian at first served Zongbi in the Eastern Secretariat and by petty cleverness won Zongbi's favor; when Zongbi held power he was brought in as vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had led troops but failed to hold the Yanshan line and ultimately ruined the Song; Yue often taunted Songnian with this. Songnian had first served Zongbi on the Eastern Secretariat staff and won his favor through petty cleverness; when Zongbi held power he was made vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 望之為尚書省都事，霖為省令史。

translations.literal: Wangzhi was chief clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and Lin was a secretariat clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi was chief clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and Lin a secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 皆怨瑴等，時時毀短之于宗弼，凡與瑴善者皆指以為朋黨。

translations.literal: They all resented Yue and others, constantly slandering them to Zongbi; everyone friendly with Yue was denounced as a faction.
translations.idiomatic: They resented Yue and his circle and constantly slandered them to Zongbi; anyone friendly with Yue was denounced as part of a faction.

sentences.zh: 韓企先疾病，宗弼往問之，是日，瑴在企先所，聞宗弼至，知其惡己，乃自屏以避。

translations.literal: Han Qixian fell ill; Zongbi went to inquire after him. That day Yue was at Qixian's residence; hearing Zongbi had come and knowing he hated him, he withdrew to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qixian fell ill, Zongbi went to visit him. Yue happened to be there that day; hearing Zongbi arrive and knowing his enmity, Yue withdrew to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼曰：「丞相年老且疾病，誰可繼丞相者？

translations.literal: Zongbi said: "The chief minister is old and ill—who can succeed him?
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi asked, "The chief minister is old and ill—who can succeed him?

sentences.zh: 」企先舉瑴，而宗弼先入松年譖言，謂企先曰：「此輩可誅。

translations.literal: " Qixian recommended Yue, but Zongbi had already been primed by Songnian's slanders and said to Qixian: "These men deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: " Qixian recommended Yue, but Zongbi had already been primed by Songnian's slanders and told him, "These men deserve death.

sentences.zh: 」瑴聞流汗浹背。

translations.literal: " When Yue heard this, sweat poured down his back.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue, overhearing, broke out in a cold sweat.

sentences.zh: 企先薨，瑴出為橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Qixian died, Yue went out as military commissioner of the Henghai army.
translations.idiomatic: After Qixian died, Yue was posted as military commissioner of the Henghai army.

sentences.zh: 選人龔夷鑒除名，值赦，赴吏部銓，得預覃恩。

translations.literal: The candidate Gong Yijian had been struck from the rolls; when an amnesty came he went to the Ministry for selection and was allowed to share in the general grace.
translations.idiomatic: The candidate Gong Yijian had been struck from the rolls; when an amnesty was declared he went to the Ministry for selection and was allowed to share in the general grace.

sentences.zh: 瑴已除橫海，部吏以夷鑒白瑴，瑴乃倒用月日署之。

translations.literal: Yue had already been appointed to Henghai; a department clerk reported Yijian to Yue, and Yue signed with the month and day reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had already been appointed to Henghai; a staff clerk reported Yijian's case to him, and Yue signed the order with the month and day reversed.

sentences.zh: 許霖在省典覃恩，行台省工部員外郎張子周素與瑴有怨，以事至京師，微知夷鑒覃恩事，嗾許霖發之，樉以專擅朝政。

translations.literal: Xu Lin was in charge of the general grace in the Secretariat; Zhang Zizhou, vice director of Works on the Eastern Secretariat, had long borne a grudge against Yue. Coming to the capital on business, he learned slightly of the Yijian grace affair and urged Xu Lin to expose it, posting a notice accusing them of monopolizing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Lin oversaw the general grace in the Secretariat; Zhang Zizhou of the Eastern Secretariat Works office, who bore a grudge against Yue, came to the capital on business, learned of the Yijian affair, and urged Xu Lin to expose it, accusing Yue of usurping court authority.

sentences.zh: 詔獄鞫之，擬瑴與奚毅、邢具瞻、王植、高鳳庭、王效、趙益興、龔夷鑒死，其妻子及所往來孟浩等三十四人皆徙海上，仍不以赦原。

translations.literal: An imperial prison inquiry was ordered; it proposed death for Yue with Xi Yi, Xing Juzhan, Wang Zhi, Gao Fengting, Wang Xiao, Zhao Yixing, and Gong Yijian; their wives and children and thirty-four associates including Meng Hao were all exiled to the sea coast, still not forgiven by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial prison inquiry was ordered; death was proposed for Yue, Xi Yi, Xing Juzhan, Wang Zhi, Gao Fengting, Wang Xiao, Zhao Yixing, and Gong Yijian; their families and thirty-four associates including Meng Hao were exiled to the coast, with no amnesty allowed.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The empire regarded the case as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 世宗在熙宗時，知田瑴黨事皆松年等構成之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong was under Emperor Xizong, he knew the Tian Yue faction case had all been fabricated by Songnian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Emperor Xizong, Emperor Shizong had known the Tian Yue faction case was fabricated by Songnian and his allies.

sentences.zh: 而浩等三十二人遇天德赦令還鄉里，多物故，惟浩與瑴兄谷、王補、馮煦、王中安在。

translations.literal: Hao and the other thirty-two met the Tiande amnesty and returned to their home districts; many had died, and only Hao, Yue's elder brother Gu, Wang Bu, Feng Xu, and Wang Zhong'an survived.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and thirty-one others returned home under the Tiande amnesty; many had died en route, and only Hao, Yue's elder brother Gu, Wang Bu, Feng Xu, and Wang Zhong'an survived.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，召見，複官爵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading they were summoned and their offices and titles restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading they were summoned to court and their offices and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 浩為侍御史，谷為大理丞，補為工部員外郎，煦為兵部主事，中安知火山軍事，而浩尋複為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Hao became attendant censor, Gu a judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Bu vice director of Works, Xu a secretary in the Ministry of War, Zhong'an military administrator of Huoshan, and Hao soon again became vice director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was made attendant censor, Gu a judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Bu vice director of works, Xu a secretary in the Ministry of War, and Zhong'an military administrator of Huoshan; Hao was soon restored as vice director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 浩篤實，遇事輒言，無所隱。

translations.literal: Hao was sincere and solid; when matters arose he spoke at once, concealing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was forthright and honest; whenever an issue arose he spoke his mind without concealment.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其忠，每對大臣稱之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and often spoke of him to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized his loyalty and often praised him to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 有疾，求外補，除祁州刺史，致仕，歸。

translations.literal: When ill he sought an outside appointment, was made prefect of Qi Prefecture, retired, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he sought a provincial post, was made prefect of Qi, retired, and went home.

sentences.zh: 七年，起為禦史中丞，而浩已年老，世宗以不次用之，再閱月，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was recalled as censor-in-chief; Hao was already old, but Emperor Shizong used him out of rank, and within two months he was appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled as censor-in-chief; though Hao was already old, Emperor Shizong promoted him out of rank, and within two months he was made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 故事，無自中丞拜執政者，浩辭曰：「不次之恩，非臣所敢當。

translations.literal: By precedent no one was made to the council directly from censor-in-chief; Hao declined: "Favor out of rank is not what your servant dares accept.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent no censor-in-chief had ever been made a councilor; Hao declined, saying, "Such extraordinary favor is more than I dare accept.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿自刺史致仕，除中丞，國家用人，豈拘階次？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You retired from a prefecture, were made censor-in-chief—when the state employs men, how can it be bound by rank order?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You retired as a prefect and were made censor-in-chief—when the state employs men, must it be bound by rank?

sentences.zh: 卿公正忠勤，雖年高猶可宣力數年，朕思之久矣。

translations.literal: You are upright, loyal, and diligent; though advanced in years you can still exert yourself for several years—I have thought of this long.
translations.idiomatic: You are upright, loyal, and diligent; though you are old you can still serve for years—I have had this in mind for a long time.

sentences.zh: 」浩頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Hao bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 世宗敕有司東宮涼樓增建殿位，浩諫曰：「皇太子義兼臣子，若所居與至尊宮室相侔，恐制度未宜，固宜示以儉德。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered the offices to add hall positions to the Eastern Palace cool pavilion; Hao remonstrated: "The crown prince in duty is also a subject; if his residence matches the supreme sovereign's palaces, I fear the regulations are not fitting—it is right to show him frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered additional halls built at the crown prince's summer pavilion; Hao remonstrated, "The crown prince is subject as well as heir; if his residence rivals the emperor's palaces, the regulations are wrong—he should be shown the virtue of frugality.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷其役，因謂太子曰：「朕思漢文純儉，心常慕之，汝亦可以為則也。

translations.literal: " The work was then stopped, and he told the crown prince: "I think of Emperor Wen of Han's pure frugality and always admire it in my heart—you too may take it as your model.
translations.idiomatic: " The work was halted, and he told the crown prince, "I often think of Emperor Wen of Han's pure frugality and admire it—you too should take him as your model.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，皇太子生日，上宴群臣於東宮，以大玉杓、黃金五百兩賜丞相志甯，顧謂群臣曰：「卿等能立功，朕亦褒賞如此。

translations.literal: " Before long, on the crown prince's birthday, the emperor feasted the ministers at the Eastern Palace and gave Chief Councilor Zhining a great jade ladle and five hundred taels of gold, turning to the ministers and saying: "If you can achieve merit, I too will reward you like this.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward, at the crown prince's birthday feast in the Eastern Palace, he gave Chief Councilor Zhining a great jade ladle and five hundred taels of gold and told the assembled ministers, "If you achieve merit, I will reward you just as generously.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「參政孟浩公正敢言，自中丞為執政。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Vice Councilor Meng Hao is upright and daring in speech—I made him to the council from censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Vice Councilor Meng Hao is upright and outspoken—I promoted him from censor-in-chief to the council.

sentences.zh: 卿等能如是，朕亦不次用之。

translations.literal: If you can be like this, I too will use you out of rank.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you can do the same, I will promote you out of rank as well.

sentences.zh: 」世宗嘗曰：「女直本尚純樸，今之風俗，日薄一日，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong once said: "The Jurchen originally still valued simplicity; today's customs grow thinner day by day—I deeply pity this.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizong once said, "The Jurchen once prized simplicity, but customs grow more corrupt by the day, and I deeply regret it.

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「臣四十年前在會寧，當時風俗與今日不同，誠如聖訓。

translations.literal: " Hao answered: "Forty years ago I was at Huining; the customs then were not like today's—truly as Your Sagely teaching says.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "Forty years ago I was at Huining; customs then were not what they are today—exactly as Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿舊人，固知之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You are an old hand—you naturally know it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are an old hand—you know it well.

sentences.zh: 」上謂宰臣曰：「宋前廢帝呼其叔湘東王為'豬王'，食之以牢，納之泥中，以為戲笑。

translations.literal: " The emperor told the chief ministers: "Song's deposed emperor called his uncle the Prince of Xiangdong 'Pig King,' fed him from a pen, pushed him into the mud, and made sport of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor told his ministers, "The deposed Song emperor called his uncle the Prince of Xiangdong the 'Pig King,' fed him from a sty, pushed him into the mud, and laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 書于史策，所以勸善而懲惡也。

translations.literal: It is written in the historical records to encourage good and punish evil.
translations.idiomatic: Such deeds are written in the histories to encourage good and warn against evil.

sentences.zh: 海陵以近習掌記注，記注不明，當時行事，實錄不載，眾人共知之者求訪書之。

translations.literal: Hailing had intimates keep the diary notes; the notes were unclear, and events of the time were not recorded in the Veritable Records—what everyone commonly knew should be sought out and written.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had his intimates keep the court diary, and the entries were unclear; events of his reign were omitted from the Veritable Records—what everyone knew should be sought out and recorded.

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「良史直筆，君舉必書。

translations.literal: " Hao answered: "A good historian writes straight—the ruler's every act is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "A good historian writes without fear—the ruler's every act is recorded.

sentences.zh: 帝王不自觀史，記注之臣乃得盡其直筆。

translations.literal: When emperors and kings do not themselves read the history, the diarists can fully wield their straight brush.
translations.idiomatic: Only when emperors do not read the history themselves can the diarists write with full honesty.

sentences.zh: 」浩複奏曰：「曆古以來，不明賞罰而能治者，未之聞也。

translations.literal: " Hao again memorialized: "From antiquity until now, I have never heard of one who could govern without clear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao further memorialized, "From antiquity until now I have never heard of a ruler who could govern without clear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 國家賞善罰惡，蓋亦多矣，而天下莫能知。

translations.literal: The state rewards good and punishes evil—there are indeed many such cases—but all under Heaven cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: The state rewards the good and punishes the wicked in many cases, yet the empire does not hear of them.

sentences.zh: 乞自今凡賞功罰罪，皆具事狀頒告之，使君子知勸以遷善，小人知懼以自警。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on every reward for merit and punishment for crime set forth the facts and be proclaimed, so gentlemen know encouragement to move toward good and petty men know fear to warn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth every reward and punishment be announced with a full statement of the facts, so that gentlemen are encouraged toward virtue and petty men are warned to restrain themselves.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 進尚書右丞，兼太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 罷為真定尹，上曰：「卿年雖老，精神不衰，善治軍民，毋遽言退。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be prefect of Zhending; the emperor said: "Though your years are many, your spirit does not decline—govern troops and people well and do not hurry to speak of withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved and made prefect of Zhending; the emperor said, "Though you are old, your spirit is undiminished—govern the troops and people well and do not be quick to speak of retirement.

sentences.zh: 」以通犀帶賜之。

translations.literal: " He was given a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 十三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 附 田瑴

translations.literal: Appended: Tian Yue
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Tian Yue

sentences.zh: 田瑴自大理丞累官同知中京留守，終於利涉軍節度使。

translations.literal: Tian Yue rose from judge of the Court of Judicial Review through successive offices to acting Central Capital garrison commander, ending as military commissioner of the Lishe army.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue rose from judge of the Court of Judicial Review through successive posts to acting garrison commander of the Central Capital and ended as military commissioner of the Lishe army.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，章宗詔尚書省曰：「故吏部侍郎田瑴等皆中正之士，小人以朋黨陷之，由是得罪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Emperor Zhangzong edicted the Imperial Secretariat: "The late Vice Minister of Personnel Tian Yue and others were all upright men whom petty men trapped as a faction, and thereby they were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Emperor Zhangzong ordered the Imperial Secretariat, "The late Vice Minister of Personnel Tian Yue and others were upright men whom petty men destroyed as a faction, and so they were punished.

sentences.zh: 世宗用孟浩為右丞，當時在者俱已用之，亡者未加追複，其議以聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong employed Meng Hao as right vice director; those then living were all used, but the dead were not yet posthumously restored—submit your deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had employed Meng Hao as right vice director; those who survived were all re-employed, but the dead had not been posthumously restored—report your deliberations.

sentences.zh: 」張汝霖奏曰：「瑴專權樹黨，先朝已正罪名，莫不稱當。

translations.literal: " Zhang Rulin memorialized: "Yue monopolized power and built a faction; the previous court already fixed their crimes, and none failed to call it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Rulin memorialized, "Yue monopolized power and built a faction; the previous court already fixed their guilt, and everyone agreed it was just.

sentences.zh: 今追贈官爵，恐無懲勸。

translations.literal: To posthumously grant offices and titles now—I fear there will be no warning or encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: To posthumously restore their titles now would destroy any deterrent effect.

sentences.zh: 」汝霖先朝大臣，嘗與顧命，上初即位，不肯輒逆其意，謂之曰：「卿既以為不可，姑置之。

translations.literal: " Rulin was a minister of the previous court who had shared the deathbed charge; when the emperor first took the throne he would not lightly oppose him and said: "Since you think it cannot be done, for now set it aside.
translations.idiomatic: " Rulin was a former minister who had shared the deathbed charge; the new emperor would not lightly oppose him and said, "Since you object, leave the matter for now.

sentences.zh: 」蓋張浩與蔡松年友善，故汝霖猶擠之也。

translations.literal: " This was because Zhang Hao was friendly with Cai Songnian, so Rulin still pressed against it.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Hao had been friendly with Cai Songnian, which is why Rulin still opposed the restoration.

sentences.zh: 汝霖死後，章宗複詔尚書省曰：「蓋自田瑴黨事之後，有官者以為戒，惟務苟且，習以成風。

translations.literal: After Rulin died, Zhangzong again edicted the Imperial Secretariat: "Since the Tian Yue faction affair, officeholders have taken it as a warning and only pursue expediency—a habit become custom.
translations.idiomatic: After Rulin died, Zhangzong again ordered the Imperial Secretariat, "Since the Tian Yue faction affair, officials have taken warning and pursued only expediency until it became custom.

sentences.zh: 先帝知瑴等無罪，錄用生存之人，有擢至宰執者，其次有為節度、防禦、刺史者。

translations.literal: The late emperor knew Yue and others were guiltless; he employed those who survived, some raised to the council, others made military commissioners, defense commissioners, or prefects.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor knew Yue and the others were innocent; he employed the survivors, some to the council, others as military commissioners, defense commissioners, or prefects.

sentences.zh: 其死者猶未追複，子孫猶在編戶，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: The dead have still not been posthumously restored; their descendants are still on the household registers—I deeply pity this.
translations.idiomatic: The dead have not been posthumously restored and their descendants remain on the common registers—I deeply pity them.

sentences.zh: 惟旌賢顯善，無間存沒，宜推先帝所以褒錄忠直之意，並加恩恤，以勵風俗。

translations.literal: In honoring the worthy and displaying good, without distinction between living and dead, we should extend the late emperor's intent to praise and record the loyal and upright, and together add grace and relief to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: In honoring the worthy, living or dead, we should carry forward the late emperor's intent to reward the loyal and upright, grant them favor, and thereby improve public morals.

sentences.zh: 據田瑴一起人除已敘用外，但未經任用身死，並與復舊官爵。

translations.literal: According to the Tian Yue group, apart from those already given appointments, all who died before receiving appointment are to have their former offices and titles restored.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from members of the Tian Yue group already re-employed, all who died before receiving appointment shall have their former offices and titles restored.

sentences.zh: 其子孫當時已有官職，以父祖坐党因而削除者，亦與追複。

translations.literal: Their descendants who then already held office but were struck off because fathers and grandfathers were punished as faction members are also to be posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants who had held office but were removed because their fathers or grandfathers were punished in the faction case shall also be restored.

sentences.zh: 應合追複爵位人等子孫不及廕敘者，亦皆量與恩例。」

translations.literal: Where descendants of those whose ranks should be posthumously restored did not reach yin privilege, all are to be granted grace by measure."
translations.idiomatic: Where descendants of those entitled to restoration did not receive inherited privilege, they shall all be granted favor as appropriate."

sentences.zh: 梁肅，字孟容，奉聖州人。

translations.literal: Liang Su, style name Mourong, was a native of Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Su, whose style name was Mourong, came from Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自幼勤學，夏夜讀書，往往達旦，母葛氏常滅燭止之。

translations.literal: From youth he studied diligently; on summer nights he read, often until dawn, and his mother Lady Ge often extinguished the lamp to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he studied hard; on summer nights he often read until dawn, and his mother Lady Ge would snuff the lamp to make him stop.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，擢進士第，調平遙縣主簿，遷望都、絳縣令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as registrar of Pingyao County, and transferred to be magistrate of Wangdu and Jiang counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan he passed the jinshi examination, served as registrar of Pingyao County, and was transferred to magistrate of Wangdu and Jiang counties.

sentences.zh: 以廉，入為尚書省令史。

translations.literal: For integrity he entered the capital as a secretariat clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity won him a post as clerk in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 除定海軍節度副使，改中都警巡使，遷山東西路轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Dinghai army, changed to Central Capital patrol commissioner, and transferred to deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy military commissioner of the Dinghai army, then Central Capital patrol commissioner, and then deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 營治汴宮，肅分護役事。

translations.literal: When the Bian palaces were being built, Su shared supervision of the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian palaces were being rebuilt, Su helped supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 攝大名少尹。

translations.literal: He acted as vice prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，境內盜起，驅百姓平人陷賊中不能自辨者數千人，皆系大名獄。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong bandits arose within the borders; thousands of common people driven into the bandits and unable to clear themselves were all held in Daming prison.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenglong era bandits rose within the borders; thousands of common people driven into their ranks and unable to prove their innocence were held in the Daming jail.

sentences.zh: 肅到官，考驗得其情讞，出者十八九。

translations.literal: When Su took office he examined and obtained the true verdicts; eight or nine out of ten were released.
translations.idiomatic: When Su took office he reviewed the cases and secured the true verdicts; eight or nine out of ten were released.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，宛平趙植上書曰：「頃者，正隆任用閹寺，少府少監兼上林署令胡守忠因緣巧幸，規取民利。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading Zhao Zhi of Wanping memorialized: "Recently, in Zhenglong eunuchs were employed; the Vice Supervisor of the Palace Workshops and concurrent Director of the Imperial Park Hu Shouzhong by opportunistic cleverness sought the people's profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading Zhao Zhi of Wanping memorialized, "Under Zhenglong eunuchs were employed; Hu Shouzhong, vice supervisor of the Palace Workshops and director of the Imperial Park, used his position to squeeze profit from the people.

sentences.zh: 前薊州刺史完顏守道、前中都警巡使梁肅，勤恪清廉，願加進擢。

translations.literal: The former Ji Prefecture prefect Wanyan Shoudao and former Central Capital patrol commissioner Liang Su are diligent, respectful, and clean—I wish them advanced and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect of Ji Wanyan Shoudao and the former Central Capital patrol commissioner Liang Su are diligent and incorrupt—I ask that they be promoted.

sentences.zh: 」於是守忠落少監，守道自濱州刺史召為諫議大夫，肅中都轉運副使改大興少尹。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Shouzhong was demoted from vice supervisor; Shoudao was summoned from Bin Prefecture prefect to Remonstrating Grand Master, and Su was changed from Central Capital deputy transport commissioner to vice prefect of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouzhong was demoted from vice supervisor; Shoudao was recalled from prefect of Bin to Remonstrating Grand Master; and Su was transferred from deputy transport commissioner of the Central Capital to vice prefect of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 肅上疏言：「方今用度不足，非但邊兵耗費而已。

translations.literal: Su memorialized: "At present expenditures are insufficient—not only from border troops' consumption.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized, "Expenditures are insufficient today, and not only because of border armies.

sentences.zh: 吏部以常調除漕司僚佐，皆年老資高者為之，類不稱職。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel assigns transport-office assistants by routine transfer—all are old in years and high in seniority, and mostly unfit for duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel fills transport-office posts by routine transfer with the oldest and most senior men, who are mostly unfit for the work.

sentences.zh: 臣謂凡軍功、進士諸科、門廕人，知錢谷利害，能使國用饒足而不傷民者，許上書自言。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes that all men of military merit, jinshi of various examinations, and yin privilege who understand the profit and harm of revenue and grain and can make state use abundant without harming the people be allowed to memorialize on their own behalf.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that men of military merit, jinshi of various examinations, and yin privilege who understand fiscal affairs and can enrich the treasury without harming the people be allowed to submit memorials on their own behalf.

sentences.zh: 就擇其可用，授以職事。

translations.literal: Then choose those who can be used and grant them duties.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the able among them and assign them duties.

sentences.zh: 每五年委吏部通校有無水旱屯兵，視其增耗而黜陟之。

translations.literal: Every five years entrust the Ministry to review comprehensively drought, flood, and garrison troops, and promote or demote according to increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Every five years the Ministry should review drought, flood, and garrison costs and promote or demote officials according to results.

sentences.zh: 自漢武帝用桑弘羊始立榷酤法，民間粟麥歲為酒所耗者十常二三。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu of Han employing Sang Hongyang, the monopoly wine law was first established; of the people's yearly grain and wheat, one or two tenths in three are consumed by wine.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Emperor Wu of Han employed Sang Hongyang and established the wine monopoly, two or three tenths of the people's yearly grain and wheat have been consumed in brewing.

sentences.zh: 宜禁天下酒麴，自京師及州郡官務，仍舊不得酤販出城。

translations.literal: It is fitting to prohibit brewer's grain throughout the realm; in the capital and at prefectural and circuit government monopolies, selling outside the walls must as before not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed banning brewer's grain empire-wide; at the capital and at prefectural government monopolies, wine should as before be barred from sale outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 其縣鎮鄉村，權行停止。

translations.literal: In counties, market towns, and villages, it should be provisionally halted.
translations.idiomatic: In counties, market towns, and villages, the monopoly should be suspended for the time being.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐捕蝗不如期，貶川州刺史，削官一階，解職。

translations.literal: In the third year, for failing to catch locusts on schedule, he was demoted to prefect of Chuanzhou, reduced one grade in rank, and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was demoted to prefect of Chuanzhou and stripped of one rank for failing to complete locust control on schedule, and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 上禦便殿，召左諫議大夫奚籲、翰林待制劉仲誨，秘書少監移剌子敬，訪問古今事。

translations.literal: The emperor held court in the side hall, summoned Left Remonstrating Grand Master Xi Yu, Hanlin awaiting-edict Liu Zhonghui, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Yila Zijing, and inquired into affairs ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held audience in the side hall and summoned Left Remonstrating Grand Master Xi Yu, Hanlin awaiting-edict Liu Zhonghui, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Yila Zijing to discuss affairs past and present.

sentences.zh: 少間，籲從容請曰：「梁肅材可惜，解職太重。

translations.literal: After a little while Xi Yu calmly petitioned: "Liang Su's talent is regrettable to waste; dismissal from office is too severe.
translations.idiomatic: After a while Xi Yu said calmly, "Liang Su's talent is too good to waste—the dismissal was too harsh.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」乃除河北東路轉運副使。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was appointed deputy transport commissioner of the Hebei East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " Su was then appointed deputy transport commissioner of the Hebei East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡亂後，兵食不足，詔肅措置沿邊兵食。

translations.literal: At this time, after the Wohe rebellion, military provisions were insufficient; the emperor ordered Su to arrange border military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wohe rebellion military supplies ran short, and the court ordered Su to organize provisions along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 移牒肇州、北京、廣甯鹽場，許民以米易鹽，兵民皆得其利。

translations.literal: He sent dispatches to the Zhao, Beijing, and Guangning salt works, allowing the people to exchange grain for salt; soldiers and civilians all gained the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He notified the salt offices at Zhao, Beijing, and Guangning to let people trade grain for salt, to the benefit of troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 四年，通檢東平、大名兩路戶籍物力，稱其平允。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he conducted comprehensive inspection of household registers and property assessments in the Dongping and Daming circuits; they praised his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he inspected household registers and property assessments in the Dongping and Daming circuits and was praised for fairness.

sentences.zh: 他使者所至皆以苛刻增益為功，百姓訴苦之。

translations.literal: Other envoys wherever they went all took harsh increase as merit; the people complained of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Other inspectors everywhere inflated assessments harshly to claim credit, and the people protested bitterly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷敕諸路以東平、大名通檢為准，於是始定。

translations.literal: The court ordered all circuits to take the Dongping and Daming inspections as standard; thence it was first settled.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered all circuits to follow the Dongping and Daming model, and the standard was fixed.

sentences.zh: 七年，父憂去官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he left office for father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 起複都水監。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning as Director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning to serve as Director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 河決李固，詔肅視之，還奏：「決河水六分，舊河水四分。

translations.literal: The river broke at Liguo; the emperor ordered Su to inspect it; returning he reported: "The breach river carries six parts, the old river four parts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Liguo, the emperor sent Su to inspect it; on his return he reported, "Six-tenths of the flow now runs through the breach and four-tenths through the old channel.

sentences.zh: 今障塞決河，複故道為一，再決而南則南京憂，再決而北則山東、河北皆可憂。

translations.literal: If we now dam the breach and restore the old channel as one, another break to the south would threaten Nanjing, another to the north would threaten Shandong and Hebei alike.
translations.idiomatic: If we dam the breach and force the river back into a single channel, another break to the south would endanger Nanjing, and another to the north would threaten Shandong and Hebei alike.

sentences.zh: 不若止于李固南築堤，使兩河分流，以殺水勢便。

translations.literal: Better to stop at building a dike south of Liguo and let the two rivers divide the flow, to reduce the water's force expediently.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to build a dike south of Liguo and let the two channels carry the flow separately, easing the force of the water.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 改大理卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尚輦局本把石抹阿裏哥與釘鉸匠陳外兒共盜宮中造車銀釘葉，肅以阿裏哥監臨，當首坐。

translations.literal: The Palace Chariot Bureau head corporal Shimao Alige and nail-smith Chen Wai'er together stole silver nail leaves for palace cart-making; Su held Alige as overseer and liable as principal offender.
translations.idiomatic: Shimao Alige, head corporal of the Palace Chariot Bureau, and nail-smith Chen Wai'er had together stolen silver fittings for palace carts; Su ruled that Alige, as supervisor, bore principal guilt.

sentences.zh: 他寺官以陳外兒為首，抵死。

translations.literal: Other court officials made Chen Wai'er principal and imposed death.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at other bureaus made Chen Wai'er the principal offender and sought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「罪疑惟輕，各免死，徒五年，除名。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When guilt is doubtful, favor the lighter; each spared death, penal servitude five years, names struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In doubtful cases favor the lighter penalty—spare them death, sentence each to five years' penal servitude, and strike their names from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 」于時，東京久不治，上自擇肅為同知東京留守事。

translations.literal: " At this time Eastern Capital had long gone ungoverned; the emperor himself chose Su as associate Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: " Eastern Capital had long been poorly governed; the emperor personally chose Su as associate regent there.

sentences.zh: 遷中都都轉運使，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Capital chief transport commissioner, then to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief transport commissioner of the Central Capital, then appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上疏論台諫，其大旨謂：「台官自大夫至監察，諫官自大夫至拾遺，陛下宜親擇，不可委之宰相，恐樹私恩，塞言路也。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the Censorate and remonstrance offices, the gist being: "Censorate officials from grand master to investigating censor, remonstrance officials from grand master to collector of omissions—the Your Majesty should personally select them and not entrust this to the chief councillor, lest private favor be planted and the avenue of speech blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized on the Censorate and remonstrance offices, arguing that the emperor should personally select censors and remonstrators at every rank rather than leave the choice to the chief councillor, lest private favors block the path of frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended the advice and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 複請奴婢不得服羅，上曰：「近已禁奴婢服明金矣，可漸行之。

translations.literal: Again he requested that slave women and servants must not wear silk gauze; the emperor said: "Recently slave women and servants wearing bright gold has been forbidden; this can be carried out gradually.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked that servants be forbidden to wear gauze silk; the emperor said, "We have already forbidden servants to wear bright gold—this can be phased in gradually.

sentences.zh: 」肅舉同安主簿高旭，除平陽酒使，肅奏曰：「明君用人，必器使之。
