translations.literal: " Su recommended Tong'an registrar Gao Xu; he was appointed Pingyang wine commissioner; Su memorialized: "An enlightened lord employing men must match vessel to use.
translations.idiomatic: " Su had recommended Tong'an registrar Gao Xu, who was appointed wine commissioner of Pingyang; Su objected, "A wise ruler assigns each man to a role that fits his abilities.

sentences.zh: 旭儒士，優於治民，若使坐列肆，榷酒酤，非所能也。

translations.literal: Xu is a Confucian scholar, superior at governing the people; if made to sit in market stalls monopolizing wine sales, that is not within his power.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu is a scholar better suited to governing people than to sitting in a shop running the wine monopoly—he is not fit for that work.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為諸道鹽鐵使依舊文武參注，其酒稅使副以右選三差俱最者為之。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the various circuit salt and iron commissioners should as before have civil and military jointly appointed; wine-tax deputy commissioners should be those ranked highest in three rounds of the right selection.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest that circuit salt and iron commissioners continue to be drawn from both civil and military ranks, while wine-tax deputies should be chosen from those who rank highest in three successive evaluations of the right-hand selection process.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good.

sentences.zh: 」改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: " He was changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 宋主屢請免立受國書之儀，世宗不從。

translations.literal: The Song ruler repeatedly requested exemption from the standing ceremony of receiving the state letter; Emperor Shizong did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor repeatedly asked to be excused from standing to receive the Jin state letter in person; Emperor Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 及大興尹璋為十四年正旦使，宋主使人就館奪其書，而重賂之。

translations.literal: When Daxing vice prefect Zhang was New Year's envoy in the fourteenth year, the Song ruler sent men to the lodging to seize his letter, yet heavily bribed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Prefect Zhang of Daxing went as New Year's envoy in the fourteenth year, the Song emperor had men seize the state letter at his lodge while showering him with heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 璋還，杖一百五十，除名。

translations.literal: Zhang returned, was beaten one hundred fifty strokes, and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhang was beaten one hundred fifty strokes and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 以肅為宋國詳問使，其書略曰：「盟書所載，止於帝加皇字，免奉表稱臣稱名再拜，量減歲幣，便用舊儀，親接國書。

translations.literal: Su was appointed detailed inquiry envoy to Song; the letter in summary said: "What the alliance document records stops at adding 'emperor' to the title, exempting presenting memorials with 'subject' and personal name and double bow, reducing annual tribute by measure, using the former ceremony, personally receiving the state letter.
translations.idiomatic: Su was appointed envoy to inquire of the Song; his letter in essence read, "The treaty provides only that the Song emperor's title include the character for emperor, that he be spared memorial submission with 'your subject,' his personal name, and double obeisance, that tribute be reduced, that former ceremony be used, and that he receive our state letter in person.

sentences.zh: 茲禮一定，於今十年。

translations.literal: This ceremony once fixed, it is now ten years.
translations.idiomatic: That ceremony has been settled for ten years now.

sentences.zh: 今知歲元國信使到彼，不依禮例引見，輒令迫取于館，侄國禮體當如是耶？

translations.literal: Now we know the New Year credence envoy on arriving there was not introduced by ritual precedent; they were abruptly forced to surrender it at the lodge—is a nephew state's ritual propriety to be thus?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when this year's New Year credence envoy arrived, you did not receive him by ritual precedent but had the letter seized at his lodge—should a nephew state treat its uncle's envoy so?

sentences.zh: 往問其詳，宜以誠報。

translations.literal: Go inquire the details; you should report with sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Go and inquire into the matter; answer honestly.

sentences.zh: 」肅至宋，宋主一一如約，立接國書。

translations.literal: " Su reached Song; the Song ruler wholly followed the pact, standing to receive the state letter.
translations.idiomatic: " In Song the emperor complied in full and stood to receive the state letter.

sentences.zh: 肅還，附書謝，其略曰：「侄宋皇帝謹再拜，致書于叔大金應天興祚欽文廣武仁德聖孝皇帝闕下。

translations.literal: Su returned; attached was a letter of thanks, in summary: "Nephew Song emperor reverently bows again, addressing a letter to uncle Great Jin Emperor of Heaven-responding Fortune-Raising Mandate, Admirer of Culture, Expander of Arms, Benevolent in Virtue, Holy in Filial Piety, below the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On his return a thank-you letter was attached, reading in part, "Nephew, the Song emperor, bows again and again and addresses this letter to uncle, the Great Jin emperor—Heaven's Mandate, Fortune Raised, Culture Exalted, Arms Magnified, Benevolent in Virtue, Sacred in Filial Piety—below your exalted throne.

sentences.zh: 惟十載遵盟之久，無一毫成約之違，獨顧禮文，宜存折衷。

translations.literal: Only that ten years' observance of the alliance—without the slightest breach of the settled pact—yet considering ritual text alone, there ought to be a reserved mean.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years we have kept the alliance without the slightest breach of our agreements; on ritual forms alone, allowance should be made.

sentences.zh: 矧辱函封之貺，尚循躬受之儀，既俯迫於輿情，嘗屢伸於誠請，因歲元之來使，遂商榷以從權。

translations.literal: Moreover disgraced by the sealed gift in a letter, yet still following the ceremony of receiving in person—having bowed to public sentiment, having repeatedly extended sincere requests, because of the New Year envoy came, then discussed to follow expedient weight.
translations.idiomatic: Honored by your sealed dispatch, we nevertheless tried to follow the ceremony of receiving it in person; bowing to public sentiment and our repeated sincere requests, we discussed the matter with your New Year's envoy and agreed on an expedient compromise.

sentences.zh: 敢勞將命之還，先布鄙悰之懇，自余專使肅控請祈。

translations.literal: Daring to trouble the return of the commissioned envoy, first set forth this humble sincerity's earnest plea; the rest a special envoy Su will report in petition and prayer.
translations.idiomatic: I take the liberty of conveying through the envoy you sent this humble plea in advance; a special envoy will follow to present our remaining requests.

sentences.zh: 」肅還至泗州，先遣都管趙王府長史駝滿蒲馬入奏。

translations.literal: " Su returned to Sizhou, first dispatching Chief Controller Zhao Prince's chief steward Tuoman Puma to enter and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: " Su reached Sizhou on his return and first sent Chief Controller and Zhao Prince chief steward Tuoman Puma to report to court.

sentences.zh: 世宗大喜，欲以肅為執政，左丞相良弼曰：「梁肅可相，但使宋還即為之，宋人自此輕我矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong greatly rejoiced and wished to make Su chief councillor; Left Chief Councillor Liangbi said: "Liang Su can be prime minister, but to make him so as soon as he returns from Song—the Song people from this will slight us.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was delighted and wished to make Su chief councillor; Left Chief Councillor Liangbi said, "Liang Su is fit to serve as prime minister, but if you appoint him the moment he returns from Song, the Song will henceforth despise us.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 久之，為濟南尹，上疏曰：「刑罰世輕世重，自漢文除肉刑，罪至徒者帶鐐居役，歲滿釋之，家無兼丁者，加杖准徒。

translations.literal: After a long while he was Jinan intendant; he memorialized: "Punishments in the world are light or heavy by era; from Han Wen abolishing mutilation, crimes reaching penal servitude wore shackles and performed labor, released at year's end; households without an extra adult male—added beating in lieu of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became intendant of Jinan and memorialized, "Punishments have varied in severity from age to age; since Emperor Wen of Han abolished mutilation, those sentenced to penal servitude wore shackles and labored until the term ended, with beating added in place of servitude for households without a spare adult male.

sentences.zh: 今取遼季之法，徒一年者杖一百，是一罪二刑也，刑罰之重，於斯為甚。

translations.literal: Now taking Liao late-period law, one year of servitude gets one hundred strokes—one crime, two punishments; severity of punishment, in this it is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: We now follow late Liao law, under which one year of servitude carries one hundred strokes of the rod—one crime, two punishments—and never was the penalty heavier.

sentences.zh: 今太平日久，當用中典，有司猶用重法，臣實痛之。

translations.literal: Now peace is long-established; the moderate code ought to be used, yet the offices still use heavy law—I truly grieve this.
translations.idiomatic: After so long a peace we should apply the middle standard of punishment, yet the offices still apply harsh law, which grieves me greatly.

sentences.zh: 自今徒罪之人，止居作，更不決杖，」不報。

translations.literal: From now persons guilty of servitude crimes only perform labor, no further deciding the rod," no response.
translations.idiomatic: From now on let those guilty of servitude crimes labor only and no longer be beaten with the rod." The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，起複彰德軍節度使，召拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he retired; recalled from mourning as military commissioner of Zhangde army; summoned and appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired, then was recalled from mourning as military commissioner of the Zhangde army and summoned to serve as vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「梁肅以治入異等，遂至大任，廉吏亦可以勸矣。

translations.literal: The emperor told attendant officials: "Liang Su by governance entering extraordinary grade rose to great appointment—honest officials too may be encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants, "Liang Su's excellence in governance earned him extraordinary promotion to high office—honest officials can take heart from his example.

sentences.zh: 」肅奏：「漢之羽林，皆通《孝經》。

translations.literal: " Su memorialized: "Han's Huben Guard all mastered the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "The Han Huben Guard all studied the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 今之親軍，即漢之羽林也。

translations.literal: Today's Imperial Guard are the Han Huben Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Our Imperial Guard today are the Han Huben Guard in function.

sentences.zh: 臣乞每百戶賜《孝經》一部，使之教讀，庶知臣子之道，其出職也，可知政事。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to grant one Classic of Filial Piety per hundred households, have them teach reading, that they may know the way of subject and son; when they leave office, they may understand state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each company of a hundred households be given a copy of the Classic of Filial Piety and taught to read it, so they may learn the duties of a subject; when they leave service they will better understand governance.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善，人之行，莫大於孝，亦由教而後能。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good—a man's conduct, none greater than filial piety; this too is only through teaching that one can achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good—no conduct surpasses filial piety, and only through teaching can men achieve it.

sentences.zh: 」詔與護衛俱賜焉。

translations.literal: " An edict granted it together with the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that the Guards receive copies as well.

sentences.zh: 複上奏曰：「方今斗米三百，人已困餓，以錢難得故也。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized: "At present a dou of rice is three hundred cash; people are already suffering hunger, because cash is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, "A dou of rice now costs three hundred cash and the people are starving because money is so scarce.

sentences.zh: 計天下歲入二千萬貫以上，一歲之用餘千萬。

translations.literal: Calculating the realm's yearly intake at more than twenty million strings, one year's expenditure leaves more than ten million.
translations.idiomatic: The empire takes in more than twenty million strings a year, yet after a year's spending more than ten million remain in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 院務坊場及百姓合納錢者，通減數百萬。

translations.literal: Monopoly bureaus and workshops and among the people those who ought to pay cash—in total reduce by several million.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by several million the cash owed by monopoly bureaus, workshops, and common taxpayers alike.

sentences.zh: 院務坊場可折納穀帛 ，折支官兵俸給，使錢布散民間，稍稍易得。

translations.literal: Monopoly bureaus and workshops may pay in grain and cloth as substitute; disburse military and official salaries thereby, so that cash spreads among the people and is gradually easier to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Let bureaus and workshops pay in grain and cloth, use it to pay troop and official salaries, and spread coin among the people so cash becomes easier to obtain.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「懸欠院務，許折納，可也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Outstanding debts of monopoly bureaus—allowing substitute payment, acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "For bureaus with outstanding debts, substitute payment may be allowed."

sentences.zh: 肅上疏論生財舒用八事。

translations.literal: Su memorialized discussing eight matters of generating wealth and easing expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized on eight measures to increase revenue and ease fiscal pressure.

sentences.zh: 一曰罷隨司通事；

translations.literal: First, abolish the circuit liaison clerks;
translations.idiomatic: First, abolish the circuit liaison clerks;

sentences.zh: 二曰罷酒稅司杓欄人；

translations.literal: Second, abolish the wine-tax bureau ladle-gate men;
translations.idiomatic: Second, abolish the wine-tax bureau ladle-gate men;

sentences.zh: 三曰天水郡王本族已無在者，其餘皆遠族，可罷養濟；

translations.literal: Third, of the Tian Shui Prince's clan none of the main line remain; the rest are distant kin—maintenance support may be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Tian Shui Prince's main line is extinct and the survivors are distant kin—their maintenance stipends may be abolished;

sentences.zh: 四曰裁減隨司契丹吏員；

translations.literal: Fourth, reduce Khitan clerks attached to circuit offices;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, cut the Khitan clerks attached to circuit offices;

sentences.zh: 五曰罷榷醋，以利與民；

translations.literal: Fifth, abolish the vinegar monopoly to benefit the people;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, abolish the vinegar monopoly for the people's benefit;

sentences.zh: 六曰量減鹽價，使私鹽不行，民不犯法；

translations.literal: Sixth, reduce salt prices by measure so private salt does not circulate and the people do not break the law;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, lower salt prices moderately so private salt cannot compete and the people need not violate the law;

sentences.zh: 七曰隨路酒稅許折納諸物；

translations.literal: Seventh, along each route allow wine tax to be paid in various goods as substitute;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, allow wine taxes on each circuit to be paid in kind;

sentences.zh: 八曰今歲大稔，乞廣糴粟麥，使錢貨流出。

translations.literal: Eighth, this year the harvest is great—I beg broadly to purchase grain and wheat so currency flows out.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, with this year's abundant harvest, buy grain and wheat widely so money circulates into the countryside.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「趙氏養濟一事，乃國家美政，不可罷。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Zhao clan maintenance is a beautiful policy of the state; it cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Support for the Zhao clan is a fine state policy and must not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 其七事，宰相詳議以聞。

translations.literal: As for the seven other matters, the chief councillors are to deliberate in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: The other seven proposals the chief councillors should review in detail and report.

sentences.zh: 」上又曰：「朕在位二十餘年，鑒海陵之失，屢有改作，亦不免有繆戾者，卿等悉心奏之。

translations.literal: " The emperor also said: "I have been on the throne more than twenty years, taking Hailing's failures as a mirror, repeatedly making reforms, yet not free of errors—report fully.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor added, "I have reigned more than twenty years, taking Hailing's failures as my lesson and reforming again and again, yet I am not free of mistakes—report to me with full candor.

sentences.zh: 」肅論「正員官被差，權攝官有公罪，及正員還任，皆准去官勿論，往往其人苟且，不事其事。

translations.literal: " Su argued that when regular officials are on detail assignment and acting officials commit public crimes, and when regular officials return—all treated as leaving office without consequence—those men often become negligent and neglect their duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Su argued that when a regular official is on detached duty and an acting substitute commits a public offense, the case is dismissed once the regular official returns, so men often grow careless and neglect their work.

sentences.zh: 乞于縣令中留十人備差，無差正員官。

translations.literal: Request to keep ten among county magistrates as reserve for assignment, not assign regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that ten county magistrates be kept in reserve for temporary assignments rather than sending regular incumbents.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「自今權攝有公罪，正員雖還而本職未替者，勿以去官論之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "From now when acting officials have public crimes, even if regular officials return but their post is not yet replaced, do not treat as leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "From now on, if an acting official commits a public offense, do not dismiss the case as 'left office' even when the regular official has returned but not yet been replaced.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Truly as the sacred edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "Indeed, as Your Majesty commands.

sentences.zh: 」肅與宰相奏事，既罷，肅跪而言曰：「四時畋獵，雖古禮，聖人亦以為戒。

translations.literal: " Su and the chief councillors finished reporting affairs; when done Su knelt and said: "The four seasons' hunting, though ancient ritual, the sages also took it as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " After Su and the chief councillors had finished their business, Su knelt and said, "Seasonal hunting was ancient ritual, yet even the sages warned against it.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋高，屬時嚴寒，馳聘于山林之間。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years are advanced; it happens to be severe cold—galloping amid mountain forests.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is advanced in years, and the season is bitterly cold—yet you gallop through the mountain forests.

sentences.zh: 法宮燕處，亦足怡神，願為宗社自重，天下之福也。

translations.literal: Dwelling at ease in the law palace is also enough to delight the spirit—I wish for the sake of the altars of state to value yourself; it is the fortune of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Resting peacefully in the inner palace would suffice to refresh your spirits; for the sake of the realm, guard your health—that would bless the empire.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕諸子方壯，使之習武，故時一往爾。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "My sons are just in their prime; I have them practice arms, so I go out from time to time—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "My sons are just coming of age; I take them out now and then to train in arms—that is all."

sentences.zh: 同知震武軍節度使鄧秉鈞陳言四事，其一言外多闕官，及循資擬注不得人，上以問宰相張汝弼，曰：「循資格行已久，仍舊便。

translations.literal: Associate military commissioner of the Zhenwu army Deng Bingjun presented four points; the first said that outside there are many vacant posts, and appointments by seniority alone do not obtain the right men; the emperor asked chief councillor Zhang Rubi, who said: "Seniority appointment has long been practiced; continuing as before is fine.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Bingjun, associate military commissioner of the Zhenwu army, presented four proposals; the first noted many vacant posts abroad and that appointments by seniority alone fail to secure capable men. The emperor asked Chief Councillor Zhang Rubi, who said, "Seniority has long governed appointments; let it continue as before.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Su said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 如亡遼固不足道，其用人之法有仕及四十年無敗事，即與節度使，豈必循資哉。

translations.literal: As for the fallen Liao, it is truly not worth discussing; its method of employing men was that if one served forty years without failure, he was given a military commission—must one follow seniority?
translations.idiomatic: The fallen Liao is hardly worth citing, but its method was to grant a military commission to any man who served forty years without a blemish—need promotion follow seniority alone?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「仕四十年已衰老。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Forty years in office is already old and feeble.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "A man who has served forty years is already old.

sentences.zh: 察其政績，善者升之，後政再察之，善又升之，如此可以得人，亦無曠事。

translations.literal: Examine his administrative record; if good, promote him; examine his later administration again; if good again, promote again—thus men can be obtained and posts are not left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Review his record of governance and promote the able; review his next term and promote again if he excels—thus you will find good men without leaving posts empty.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「誠如聖訓。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Truly as the sacred instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "Indeed, as Your Majesty teaches.

sentences.zh: 」肅論盜賊不息，請無禁兵器。

translations.literal: " Su argued that bandits do not cease; he requested no prohibition on weapons.
translations.idiomatic: " Su argued that banditry never ends and asked that the ban on weapons be lifted.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「所在有兵器，其利害如何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Weapons exist everywhere—what is the benefit and harm?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Weapons are kept everywhere—what is the benefit and harm of that?"

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「他路則已，中都一路上農夫聽置之，似乎無害。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Other circuits aside, on the Central Capital route letting farmers keep them seems harmless.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "Other circuits are another matter, but on the Central Capital route letting farmers keep weapons seems harmless.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕將思之。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I shall think on it."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I will consider it."

sentences.zh: 凡使宋者，宋人致禮物，大使金二百兩，銀二千兩，副使半之，幣帛雜物稱是。

translations.literal: For all envoys to Song, the Song present gifts: the chief envoy two hundred taels of gold and two thousand taels of silver, the deputy envoy half as much, with silks and miscellaneous goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an envoy went to Song, the Song presented gifts: two hundred taels of gold and two thousand taels of silver to the chief envoy, half as much to the deputy, with silks and other goods in proportion.

sentences.zh: 及推排物力，肅自以身為執政，昔嘗使宋，所得禮物多，當為庶民率先，乃自增物力六十餘貫，論者多之。

translations.literal: When assessing property, Su himself being chief councillor and having once been envoy to Song and received many gifts, ought to set the example for the common people—he therefore increased his own assessment by more than sixty strings; many in discussion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When property assessments were revised, Su, now chief councillor and formerly envoy to Song, had received lavish gifts; to set an example for the people he added more than sixty strings to his own assessment, and many praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，肅請老，上謂宰臣曰：「梁肅知無不言，正人也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Su requested retirement; the emperor told the chief ministers: "Liang Su speaks without holding back on anything—an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Su asked to retire; the emperor told the chief ministers, "Liang Su speaks his mind on everything—he is an upright man.

sentences.zh: 卿等知而不言，朕實鄙之。

translations.literal: You who know yet do not speak—I truly despise that.
translations.idiomatic: You who know yet keep silent—I truly despise that.

sentences.zh: 雖然，肅老矣，宜從其請。

translations.literal: Even so, Su is old; his request should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Su is old; we should grant his request.

sentences.zh: 」遂再致仕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he retired a second time.
translations.idiomatic: " He retired from office again.

sentences.zh: 詔以其子汝翼為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: An edict appointed his son Ruyi Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed his son Ruyi to the post of Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading he died.

sentences.zh: 諡正憲。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhengxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Zhengxian ("Upright and Lawful").

sentences.zh: 移剌慥

translations.literal: Yila Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zhao

sentences.zh: 移剌慥，本名移敵列，契丹虞呂部人。

translations.literal: Yila Zhao, original name Yidilie, was a man of the Khitan Yulü tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zhao, whose original name was Yidilie, was a Khitan of the Yulü tribe.

sentences.zh: 通契丹、漢字，尚書省辟契丹令史，攝知除，擢右司都事。

translations.literal: He mastered Khitan and Chinese script; the Ministry of Personnel enrolled him as Khitan clerk, acting in charge of appointments, and promoted him to Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: Proficient in both Khitan and Chinese writing, he was recruited by the Ministry of Personnel as a Khitan clerk, served in an acting capacity overseeing appointments, and was promoted to Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 正隆南伐，兼領契丹、漢字兩司都事。

translations.literal: During Zhenglong's southern campaign he concurrently headed both the Khitan and Chinese departments.
translations.idiomatic: During Hailing's southern campaign he concurrently headed both the Khitan-script and Chinese-script bureaus.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，除真定少尹，入為侍御史。

translations.literal: In Dading year 2 he was made Vice Prefect of Zhending, then entered court as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was appointed Vice Prefect of Zhending and then entered the capital as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起複右司員外郎，累官陳州防禦使。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning as Vice Director of the Right Department, he rose by stages to Defender of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as Vice Director of the Right Department, he rose through successive posts to Defender of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左丞相紇石烈良弼致仕，上問：「誰可代卿者？

translations.literal: Left Chief Councillor Heshilie Liangbi retired; the emperor asked: "Who can replace you?
translations.idiomatic: When Left Chief Councillor Heshilie Liangbi retired, the emperor asked, "Who can replace you?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陳州防禦使移剌慥，清幹忠正，臣不及也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Chen Defender Yila Zhao—upright, capable, and loyal; I do not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi answered, "Yila Zhao, Defender of Chen—scrupulous, capable, and loyal. I am not his equal.

sentences.zh: 」遂召為太府監。

translations.literal: " He was therefore summoned as Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was therefore summoned and appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以按出虎等八猛安，自河南徙置大名、東平之境。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year eight meng'an including Anchuhu were moved from Henan to the borders of Daming and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, eight meng'an units, including Anchuhu's, were relocated from Henan to the borderlands of Daming and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 還為大理卿，被詔典領更定制條。

translations.literal: He returned as Grand Judge of the Court of Review and was ordered to oversee revision of the legal codes.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Grand Judge and was ordered to direct the revision of the statutes.

sentences.zh: 初，皇統間，參酌隋、唐、遼、宋律令，以為皇統制條。

translations.literal: At first, during Huangtong, Sui, Tang, Liao, and Song laws were consulted to form the Huangtong statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, during the Huangtong era, statutes were drawn up by consulting the legal codes of Sui, Tang, Liao, and Song—the Huangtong codes.

sentences.zh: 海陵虐法，率意更改，或同罪異罰，或輕重不倫，或共條重出，或虛文贅意，吏不知適從，夤緣舞法。

translations.literal: Hailing cruelly manipulated the law, changing it at will; sometimes the same crime had different punishments, or severity and leniency were unordered, or the same article appeared twice, or empty words piled on meaning; officials did not know which to follow and bent the law through connections.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had twisted the law at whim—sometimes identical crimes drew different penalties, sometimes punishments were grossly disproportionate, sometimes duplicate articles appeared, sometimes verbiage obscured the point—so clerks no longer knew which rule applied, and patronage networks flourished around the statutes.

sentences.zh: 慥取皇統舊制及海陵續降，通類校定，通其窒礙，略其繁碎。

translations.literal: Zhao took the old Huangtong codes and Hailing's subsequent additions, classified and collated them, unblocked obstructions, and trimmed redundancy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao took the old Huangtong codes together with Hailing's later supplements, classified and collated them, cleared obstructive passages, and pared away redundancy.

sentences.zh: 有例該而條不載者，用例補之。

translations.literal: Where precedent covered a case but no article recorded it, precedent was used to fill the gap.
translations.idiomatic: Where precedent covered a matter but no statute recorded it, he supplied the gap with precedent.

sentences.zh: 特闕者用律增之。

translations.literal: Where something was wholly lacking, the code was used to add it.
translations.idiomatic: Where a matter was wholly unprovided for, he added provisions from the code.

sentences.zh: 凡制律不該及疑不能參決者，取旨畫定。

translations.literal: Whatever statutes and laws did not reach and doubts could not be settled by consultation were submitted for imperial decision and marked accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the statutes and laws did not reach, and whatever doubts could not be settled by consultation, were submitted for imperial decision and marked accordingly.

sentences.zh: 凡特旨處分，及權宜條例內有可常行者，收為永格。

translations.literal: Whatever special imperial orders and expedient regulations contained provisions that could be applied permanently were collected as enduring precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Special imperial orders and expedient regulations that could be applied permanently were collected as enduring precedents.

sentences.zh: 其餘未可削去者，別為一部。

translations.literal: The rest that could not yet be cut away were set apart in a separate section.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions that could not yet be removed were set apart in a separate section.

sentences.zh: 大凡一千一百九十條，為十二卷。

translations.literal: In all there were 1,190 articles in twelve volumes.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were 1,190 articles in twelve volumes.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔頒行之，賜銀幣有差。

translations.literal: When the work was submitted, an edict ordered its promulgation and silver currency was bestowed in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was submitted, an edict ordered its promulgation, and graded rewards of silver were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，摘徙山東猛安八謀克于河北東路，置之酬斡、青狗兒兩猛安舊居之地，詔無牛耕者買牛給之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter eight Shandong meng'an and mouke were selected and moved to Hebei East Circuit, placed on the former lands of the Chouwo and Qinggou'er meng'an; an edict ordered that those without oxen for plowing were to be given oxen to buy.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter eight Shandong meng'an and mouke were selected and relocated to Hebei East Circuit, settled on the former lands of the Chouwo and Qinggou'er meng'an; an edict ordered that households without oxen for plowing were to be supplied with oxen.

sentences.zh: 攝御史大夫。

translations.literal: Acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 數月，改禦史中丞，兼同修國史，遷刑部尚書，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After several months he was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently revising the national history, promoted to Minister of Punishments, then changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrently reviser of the national history, then promoted to Minister of Punishments and transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋改大興尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prefect of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Prefect of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 駕幸上京，顯宗守國，使人諭之曰：「自大駕東巡，京尹所治甚善。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Supreme Capital, Xianzong guarded the realm; a messenger instructed him: "Since the Great Carriage toured east, the capital prefect's governance has been excellent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the Supreme Capital, Emperor Xianzong remained to guard the realm; a messenger told him, "Since the imperial procession toured east, your governance of the capital has been excellent.

sentences.zh: 我將有春水之行，當益勤乃事。

translations.literal: I am about to make a spring hunt on the waters; you should be all the more diligent in your duties.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to make a spring hunt on the waters; you should be all the more diligent in your duties.

sentences.zh: 」還以所獲鵝鴨賜之。

translations.literal: " On return he bestowed on him the geese and ducks he had taken.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he bestowed on Zhao the geese and ducks taken on the hunt.

sentences.zh: 有疾在告，遣官醫診視。

translations.literal: When ill and on leave, court physicians were sent to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill and took leave, court physicians were sent to examine him.

sentences.zh: 複為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上還自上京，以為西京留守，改臨洮尹，卒。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from the Supreme Capital he was made Western Capital Military Governor, changed to Prefect of Linzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from the Supreme Capital, Zhao was appointed Western Capital Military Governor, then transferred to Prefect of Linzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 移剌子敬

translations.literal: Yila Zijing
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zijing

sentences.zh: 移剌子敬，字同文，本名屋骨朵魯，遼五院人。

translations.literal: Yila Zijing, style Tongwen, original name Uguduru, was a native of Liao's Five Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zijing, style Tongwen, whose original name was Uguduru, was a native of Liao's Five Circuits.

sentences.zh: 曾祖霸哥，同平章事。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bage was Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bage had served as Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 父拔魯，準備任使官。

translations.literal: His father Balu was Prepared Envoy Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Balu was a Prepared Envoy Officer.

sentences.zh: 都統杲克中京，遼主西走，留拔魯督輜重，已而輜重被掠，拔魯乃自髡，逃于山林。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Gao took the Central Capital; the Liao ruler fled west; Balu was left to oversee the baggage train, but the train was soon plundered; Balu then shaved his own head and fled into the mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander-in-Chief Gao captured the Central Capital and the Liao ruler fled west, Balu was left to oversee the baggage train; the train was soon plundered, whereupon Balu shaved his own head and fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 子敬讀書好學，皇統間，特進移剌固修《遼史》，辟為掾屬。

translations.literal: Zijing loved reading and study; during Huangtong the Privy Councillor Yila Gu revised the History of Liao and enrolled him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing loved reading and study; during Huangtong, when Privy Councillor Yila Gu revised the History of Liao, Zijing was enrolled on his staff as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 《遼史》成，除同知遼州事。

translations.literal: When the History of Liao was completed he was made Vice Prefect of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the History of Liao was completed, he was appointed Vice Prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 舊本愩自有占地，歲入數百貫，州官歲取其課，地主以為例，未嘗請辯。

translations.literal: The old temple estates had long held their own land, with annual income of several hundred strings; prefectural officials took its tax each year, and the landholders took it as precedent and never petitioned to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: The old temple estates had long held their own land, yielding several hundred strings a year; prefectural officials collected its tax annually, and the landholders had taken this as precedent without ever petitioning to dispute it.

sentences.zh: 子敬曰：「已有公田，何為更取民田。

translations.literal: Zijing said: "There is already public land—why take the people's land as well?
translations.idiomatic: Zijing said, "There is already public land—why take the people's land as well?

sentences.zh: 」竟不取。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he did not take it.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，郡人請留於行台省，不許。

translations.literal: When his term ended the people of the prefecture asked that he be retained at the Branch Secretariat; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the people of the prefecture asked that he be retained at the Branch Secretariat, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，入為翰林修撰，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he entered court as Hanlin reviser and was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande he entered the capital as Hanlin reviser and was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，諸將巡邊，詔子敬監戰，軍帥以戰獲分將士，亦以遺子敬，子敬不受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong the generals toured the frontier; an edict ordered Zijing to supervise the campaign; the army commanders divided battle spoils among the troops and also offered some to Zijing, but Zijing did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenglong, when the generals toured the frontier, an edict ordered Zijing to supervise the campaign; commanders divided battle spoils among the troops and also offered a share to Zijing, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 及還，入見，海陵謂之曰：「汝家貧而不苟得，不受俘獲，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: On his return, when he was received in audience, Hailing said to him: "Your family is poor yet you do not grasp at gain; you would not accept captives—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, when he was received in audience, Hailing told him, "Your family is poor yet you do not grasp at gain; you refused captives and spoils—I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 」凡同行官僚所取者，皆沒入於官。

translations.literal: " Whatever the accompanying officials had taken was all confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Whatever his fellow officials on the mission had taken was confiscated to the state.

sentences.zh: 其後詔子敬宴賜諸部，諭之曰：「凡受進，例遣宰臣，以汝前能稱職，故特命汝。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered Zijing to feast and bestow gifts on the various tribes, instructing him: "Whenever tribute is received, a chief minister is usually sent; because you previously performed well, you are specially ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered Zijing to feast the various tribes and distribute imperial gifts, telling him, "Whenever tribute is received, a chief minister is usually sent; because you previously performed well, you are specially appointed.

sentences.zh: 」使還，遷翰林待制。

translations.literal: " On his return from the mission he was promoted to Hanlin awaiting-edict.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return from the mission he was promoted to Hanlin awaiting-edict.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，以待制同修國史。

translations.literal: In Dading year 2 he served as awaiting-edict while concurrently revising the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he served as awaiting-edict while concurrently revising the national history.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡餘黨散居諸猛安謀克中，詔子敬往撫之，仍宣諭猛安謀克，及州縣漢人，無以前時用兵相殺傷，挾怨輒害契丹人。

translations.literal: At that time remnants of the Wohe rebellion were scattered among the various meng'an and mouke; an edict ordered Zijing to go pacify them, and also to proclaim to meng'an, mouke, and Han officials of prefectures and counties that they must not, because of past warfare, kill or wound one another or, nursing grievances, harm Khitan people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time remnants of the Wohe rebellion were scattered among the various meng'an and mouke; an edict ordered Zijing to go pacify them and to proclaim to meng'an, mouke, and Han officials of prefectures and counties that they must not, because of past warfare, kill or wound one another or, nursing old grievances, harm Khitan people.

sentences.zh: 使還，改秘書少監，兼修起居注，修史如故。

translations.literal: On his return he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently revising the diary of attendance, and continued revising history as before.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently reviser of the diary of attendance, while continuing his work on the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「以汝博通古今，故以命汝。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Because you are broadly versed in past and present, you are therefore appointed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Because you are broadly versed in past and present, you are therefore appointed.

sentences.zh: 」常召入講論古今及時政利害，或至夜半。

translations.literal: " He was often summoned to discuss past and present and the benefits and harms of current policy, sometimes until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: " He was often summoned to discuss past and present and the benefits and harms of current policy, sometimes until midnight.

sentences.zh: 子敬有良馬，平章政事完顏元宜索之，子敬以元宜為相也，不與。

translations.literal: Zijing had a fine horse; Associate Grand Councillor Wanyan Yuanyi demanded it; Zijing, because Yuanyi was chief minister, would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing owned a fine horse; Associate Grand Councillor Wanyan Yuanyi demanded it, but Zijing, because Yuanyi was chief minister, refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，元宜乞致仕，罷為東京，子敬乃以此馬贐行，識者韙之。

translations.literal: At this time Yuanyi requested retirement and was dismissed to the Eastern Capital; Zijing then presented this horse as a parting gift; observers approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyi requested retirement and was sent to the Eastern Capital, Zijing then presented the horse as a parting gift; observers approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，僕散忠義伐宋，宋請和，而書式、疆界未定。

translations.literal: At that time Pusann Zhongyi attacked Song; Song sought peace, but the form of documents and the boundaries were not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pusann Zhongyi was campaigning against Song; Song sought peace, but the form of diplomatic documents and the boundaries were not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 子敬與秘書少監石抹頤、修起居注張汝弼侍便殿，上曰：「宋主求成，反覆無信，喜為誇大。

translations.literal: Zijing with Vice Director of the Secretariat Shimo Yi and diary reviser Zhang Rubi attended in the side hall; the emperor said: "The Song ruler seeks peace yet is faithless and changeable, and loves grandiloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing, with Vice Director of the Secretariat Shimo Yi and diary reviser Zhang Rubi, attended in the side hall; the emperor said, "The Song ruler seeks peace yet is faithless and changeable, and loves grandiloquence.

sentences.zh: 」子敬對曰：「宋人自來浮辭相欺，來書言海陵敗于採石，大軍北歸，按兵不襲，俾全師而還。

translations.literal: " Zijing replied: "Song men have always deceived with empty words; their letter says Hailing was defeated at Caishi, the great army returned north, held the troops and did not strike, allowing the whole force to return intact.
translations.idiomatic: " Zijing replied, "The Song have always deceived with empty words; their letter says Hailing was defeated at Caishi, the great army returned north, held its troops and did not strike, allowing the whole force to return intact.

sentences.zh: 海陵未嘗敗於採石，其譎詐多此類也。

translations.literal: Hailing was never defeated at Caishi; their deceit is mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was never defeated at Caishi; their deceit is mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 回書宜言往者大軍若令渡江，宋國境土，必為我有。

translations.literal: The reply should say that if in the past the great army had been ordered to cross the Yangzi, Song territory would certainly have been ours.
translations.idiomatic: The reply should say that if in the past the great army had been ordered to cross the Yangzi, Song territory would certainly have been ours.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「彼以詭詐，我以誠實，但當以理折之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "They use deceit; we use honesty—only refute them by reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "They use deceit; we use honesty—we need only refute them by reason.

sentences.zh: 」遷右諫議大夫，起居注如故。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, with the diary post as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, while retaining his post as diary reviser.

sentences.zh: 上幸西京，州縣官入見，猛安謀克不得隨班。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Western Capital, prefectural and county officials were received in audience, but meng'an and mouke could not follow in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Western Capital, prefectural and county officials were received in audience, but meng'an and mouke commanders could not join the ranks.

sentences.zh: 子敬奏軍民一體，合令猛安謀克隨班入見，上嘉納之，於是責讓宣徽院。

translations.literal: Zijing memorialized that army and people are one body and that meng'an and mouke ought to follow the ranks in audience; the emperor commended and accepted it, and thereupon reprimanded the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing memorialized that army and people are one body and that meng'an and mouke ought to join the ranks in audience; the emperor commended and accepted it, and thereupon reprimanded the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及端午朝會，詔依子敬奏行之。

translations.literal: At the Dragon Boat Festival court assembly an edict ordered that Zijing's memorial be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dragon Boat Festival court assembly an edict ordered that Zijing's memorial be carried out.

sentences.zh: 子敬言山后禁獵地太廣，有妨百姓耕墾，上用其言，遂以四外獵地與民。

translations.literal: Zijing said the forbidden hunting grounds north of the mountains were too broad and hindered the people's plowing and cultivation; the emperor used his words and thereupon gave the outer four hunting grounds to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing said the forbidden hunting grounds north of the mountains were too broad and hindered the people's farming; the emperor accepted his advice and gave the outer four hunting grounds to the people.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監，諫議、起居如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat; remonstrance and diary posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, while retaining his posts as remonstrator and diary reviser.

sentences.zh: 子敬舉同知宣徽院事移剌神獨斡、兵部侍郎移剌按答，太子少詹事烏古論三合自代，上不許。

translations.literal: Zijing recommended Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yila Shenduwo, Vice Minister of War Yila Anda, and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wugulun Sanhe to replace himself; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing recommended Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yila Shenduwo, Vice Minister of War Yila Anda, and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wugulun Sanhe to succeed him; the emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 子敬與同簽宣徽院事移剌神獨斡侍，上曰：「亡遼不忘舊俗，朕以為是。

translations.literal: Zijing with Associate Director of the Palace Secretariat Yila Shenduwo attended; the emperor said: "The fallen Liao did not forget old customs—I approve of that.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing attended with Associate Director of the Palace Secretariat Yila Shenduwo; the emperor said, "The fallen Liao did not forget old customs—I approve of that.

sentences.zh: 海陵習學漢人風俗，是忘本也。

translations.literal: Hailing studied Han customs—that was forgetting one's roots.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing studied Han customs—that was forgetting one's roots.

sentences.zh: 若依國家舊風，四境可以無虞，此長久之計也。

translations.literal: If one follows the state's old ways, the four borders can be without worry; this is a plan for long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: If one follows the state's old ways, the four borders can be secure; this is a plan for long endurance.

sentences.zh: 」世宗將如涼陘，子敬與右補闕粘割斡特剌、左拾遺楊伯仁奏曰：「車駕至曷裏滸，西北招討司囿於行宮之內地矣。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizong was about to go to Liangyin, Zijing with Right Supplementation Censor Nianzha Wetela and Left Reminder Yang Boren memorialized: "When the imperial carriage reaches Heli Marsh, the Northwestern Pacification Commission is enclosed within the inner grounds of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Shizong was about to go to Liangyin, Zijing with Right Supplementation Censor Nianzha Wetela and Left Reminder Yang Boren memorialized, "When the imperial carriage reaches Heli Marsh, the Northwestern Pacification Commission will lie within the inner grounds of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 乞遷之於界上，以遮罩環衛。

translations.literal: We beg that it be moved to the border to screen and guard the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that it be moved to the border to screen and guard the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good.

sentences.zh: 」詔尚書省曰：「招討斜裏虎可徙界上，治蕃部事。

translations.literal: " An edict to the Ministry of Personnel said: "Pacification Commissioner Xielihu may be moved to the border to govern tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict to the Ministry of Personnel said, "Pacification Commissioner Xielihu may be moved to the border to govern tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 都監撒八仍于燕子城治猛安謀克事。」

translations.literal: Supervisor Saba is still to govern meng'an and mouke affairs at Swallow City."
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Saba is still to govern meng'an and mouke affairs at Swallow City."

sentences.zh: 上與侍臣論古之人君賢否，子敬奏曰：「陛下凡與宰臣謀議，不可不令史官知之。

translations.literal: When the emperor discussed with attending ministers whether ancient rulers were worthy or not, Zijing memorialized: "Whenever Your Majesty deliberates with chief ministers, the historiographers must not be kept ignorant.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor discussed with attending ministers whether ancient rulers were worthy or not, Zijing memorialized, "Whenever Your Majesty deliberates with chief ministers, the historiographers must not be kept ignorant.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Your words are correct.

sentences.zh: 」轉簽書樞密院事，同修國史，出為河中尹，請老。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently revising the national history, went out as Prefect of Hezhong, and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and continued revising the national history, then went out as Prefect of Hezhong and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 河中地熱，上恐子敬不耐暑，改興中尹。

translations.literal: Hezhong was hot in climate; fearing Zijing could not endure the heat, he was changed to Prefect of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong was hot in climate; fearing Zijing could not endure the heat, the emperor transferred him to Prefect of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 子敬女自懿州來興中省謁，遇盜途中，剽掠其行李且盡，既而還之，謝曰：「我輩初不知為府尹家也，尹有德于民，尚忍侵犯邪。

translations.literal: Zijing's daughter came from Yizhou to Xingzhong to visit her family, met bandits on the road, who plundered her baggage almost entirely; afterward they returned it, apologizing: "We did not know at first that this was the prefect's household; the prefect has virtue toward the people—how could we bear to violate him?
translations.idiomatic: Zijing's daughter came from Yizhou to Xingzhong to visit her family and met bandits on the road, who plundered her baggage almost entirely; afterward they returned it, apologizing, "We did not know at first that this was the prefect's household; the prefect has virtue toward the people—how could we bear to violate him?

sentences.zh: 」徙咸平、廣甯尹。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Prefect of Xianping and Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Prefect of Xianping and Guangning.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，致仕，卒於家，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he retired from office and died at home, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he retired from office and died at home, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 子敬嘗使宋，及受諸部進貢，所受禮物，皆散之親舊。

translations.literal: Zijing had once been envoy to Song, and when he received tribute from the various tribes the gifts he received were all distributed to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing had once been envoy to Song, and when he received tribute from the various tribes the gifts he received were all distributed to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 及卒，家無餘財，其子質宅以營葬事。

translations.literal: When he died the family had no surplus wealth; his son pawned the house to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the family had no surplus wealth; his son pawned the house to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金制，尚書令、左右丞相、平章政事，是謂宰相；

translations.literal: Commentary: In Jin institutions, Ministerial Director, Left and Right Chief Councillors, and Associate Grand Councillors are called chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Under Jin institutions, the Ministerial Director, the Left and Right Chief Councillors, and the Associate Grand Councillors are called chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 左右丞、參知政事，是謂執政。

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Councillors and Participation Councillors are called participating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: the Left and Right Vice Councillors and the Participation Councillors are called participating ministers.

sentences.zh: 大抵因唐官而稍異焉，因革不同，無足疑者。

translations.literal: Broadly they followed Tang offices with slight differences; changes old and new differ—nothing to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly they followed Tang offices with slight differences; that institutions evolved differently is nothing to doubt.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "The sovereign is discerning! The assistants are good! All affairs are well governed!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "The sovereign is discerning! The assistants are good! All affairs are well governed!

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「元首叢脞哉，股肱惰哉，萬事隳哉。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The sovereign is muddled! The assistants are lazy! All affairs are ruined!
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "The sovereign is muddled! The assistants are lazy! All affairs are ruined!

sentences.zh: 」宰相、執政，豈異道邪？

translations.literal: " Are chief ministers and participating ministers a different path?
translations.idiomatic: " Are chief ministers and participating ministers on a different path?

sentences.zh: 蘇保衡、翟永固、魏子平、孟浩、梁肅皆當時之賢執政也。

translations.literal: Su Baoheng, Di Yonggu, Wei Ziping, Meng Hao, and Liang Su were all worthy participating ministers of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Su Baoheng, Di Yonggu, Wei Ziping, Meng Hao, and Liang Su were all worthy participating ministers of their time.

sentences.zh: 移剌慥、子敬有其才，適其時，而位不及者，亦命也夫。

translations.literal: Yila Zhao and Zijing had the talent and met the time, yet did not reach such rank—this too was fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zhao and Yila Zijing had the talent and met the time, yet did not reach such rank—this too was fate.
